examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a link for drawing a conclusion here.
ます requires the stem し.
な cannot be attached to the conditional.

en.meaning: taking the opportunity, at the same time
en.explanation: Expresses that one does two things at once or combines one purpose with another. This formal structure is used to show that one is using an opportunity to achieve two goals. Common in polite or business correspondence.
en.formation: Noun + かたがた / Verb ます-stem + かたがた
en.notes: Formal and polite. Often used in business letters or formal situations.
examples[].german: I came by to thank you and, at the same time, to pay my respects.
I went out shopping and took a walk at the same time.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a connecting link here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to かたがた.

en.explanation: Expresses that one carries out two activities in parallel, one being the main occupation and the other a side activity. This structure is used to describe parallel or simultaneous activities. Often used in the context of a job and a side activity.
en.formation: Noun + のかたわら / Verb 辞書形 + かたわら
en.notes: Emphasizes the simultaneity of two ongoing activities, not just one-off actions.
examples[].german: Alongside his job as an office worker, he also writes novels.
Alongside my job, I study at university.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a link for a side activity here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to かたわら.

en.explanation: Expresses an undesirable tendency of a person or group. Critical, detached and written in style; きらい (嫌い) is usually written in hiragana here.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form / ない-form) + きらいがある; Noun + の + きらいがある
en.notes: Only for negative tendencies. More neutral: ～傾向がある (tendency); more everyday: ～がち (N3). Do not confuse with 嫌い (to dislike).
examples[].german: He tends to look on the dark side of things.
It is said that young people these days tend to read less and less.
This government tends to put off problems.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 考えることがある only means "sometimes thinks that way" and does not express a criticized tendency.
わけがない ("it's impossible that") contradicts the statement.
べきだ ("should") expresses an obligation, not a tendency.

en.explanation: Expresses that something has reached an extreme degree. Often used with na-adjectives to express strong feelings or states.
en.formation:
な-adjective + 極まりない/極まる
Noun + 極まりない/極まる
en.notes: A very formal expression, often used in written language.
examples[].german: That is extremely rude behavior.
We ended up in an extremely dangerous situation.
It's an extremely dangerous plan.
I live in an extremely inconvenient place.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
No additional な comes before 行為 here.
The adverbial form does not modify 行為 attributively here.

en.meaning: admittedly ... but; if anything ... but never
en.explanation: Concedes that something goes in one direction, but rules out the opposite. A very literary expression.
en.formation:
Noun + こそあれ
Verb ます-form + こそすれ
en.notes: Very literary; not in common use in modern colloquial language.
examples[].german: It may increase, but it will never decrease.
If anything, she will get angry; she certainly won't be pleased.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を cannot connect to ある here.
な cannot be attached here.
る cannot attach to ます.

en.meaning: if anything (this way), but never the opposite
en.explanation: Similar to こそあれ; emphasizes that something tends in one direction but is definitely not the opposite. Very literary.
en.formation: Verb ます-form + こそすれ
en.notes: Very literary and formal; archaic style.
examples[].german: The difficulties will increase, if anything, rather than decrease.
His attitude is hardening, if anything, rather than softening.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を cannot connect to する here.
な cannot be attached here.
る cannot attach to ます.

en.explanation: Formal expression meaning 'without doing something'. This structure is used to express that something is achieved without carrying out a particular action. Often found in literary or academic texts.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + ことなしに
en.notes: Formal and literary. A more formal alternative to ないで or ずに.
examples[].german: Without making an effort, you cannot achieve success.
He left the room without saying a single word.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This does not form the negative condition 'without effort'.
を does not form a link expressing an accompanying circumstance here.
な cannot be attached here.

en.explanation: A written-style reason, usually to ask for leniency or to apologize: because the circumstances are such, what follows is understandable. Sounds old-fashioned and polite.
en.formation: Verb (plain form) / な-adj + な / Noun + の + こととて
en.notes: Almost only in apologies and formal letters; also with the classical negative: 慣れぬこととて. Everyday: ～ので／～ものだから. Do not confuse with ～とて on its own ("even, too", 私とて).
examples[].german: Being unaccustomed to this, I have caused you trouble.
It was only a child's doing, so please forgive him.
Because it was so sudden, we could not prepare sufficiently.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ことなく ("without ...") gives no reason.
ことか is an exclamation ("how much!") and cannot introduce a subordinate clause.
慣れないことには means "unless one gets used to it" and requires a negative consequence, not an apology.

en.meaning: then there's nothing left but to
en.explanation: Expresses that if a condition is not met, one will simply do something else. This structure is used to express an alternative solution or a fallback plan. Often carries a sense of resignation or pragmatism.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + までだ/までのことだ
en.notes: Expresses a pragmatic or resigned attitude.
examples[].german: If he doesn't come, I'll just go alone.
If it doesn't work out, I'll have no choice but to give up.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The object particle does not end the sentence.
The attributive form does not end the sentence.
ます cannot be attached directly to も.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is so obvious or simple that there is no need to do it. This structure emphasizes that an action is superfluous. Can also mean that something goes without saying.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + までもない
en.notes: Emphasizes that something is self-evident or superfluous.
examples[].german: There's no need to say something like that (it goes without saying).
Everyone understands it without any need for an explanation.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
The expression requires も instead of を.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is morally unacceptable or unworthy. This very formal and archaic structure is used to express strong moral condemnation. Mainly found in literary or very formal contexts.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + まじき + Noun
en.notes: Very formal and archaic. Expresses strong moral condemnation.
examples[].german: That is behavior unworthy of a teacher.
He committed a crime that is unforgivable for a human being.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial form cannot modify 行為 attributively here.
No additional な comes before 行為 here.
ます cannot be attached directly to まじき.

en.explanation: もさることながら expresses that while the first point mentioned is important or remarkable, the following point is even more important or remarkable. It is used to highlight two aspects, with the emphasis on the second. This construction is very formal.
en.formation: Noun + もさることながら
en.notes: Very formal. Stresses the second point more than the first.
examples[].german: Not only is his academic background impressive, he also has a wealth of practical experience.
Not only the food but also the atmosphere of this restaurant is wonderful.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を cannot come before ながら here.
な cannot be attached to this connection.
ます cannot be attached to ながら.

en.explanation: Gives an explanation or justification for an action or situation. Often expresses a subjective reason.
en.formation:
普通形 + もの
普通形 + もん (colloquial)
en.notes: Often used by women and children; sounds slightly defiant.
examples[].german: I just don't want to go.
I'm tired, after all, so I want to rest.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ます cannot attach directly to もの.
No な comes before です here.
ます cannot attach to を.

en.explanation: Expresses regret or dissatisfaction about a situation that could have been different. This structure is used to show that reality does not match expectations. Often placed at the end of a sentence, with a sense of disappointment.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/た-form + ものを / い-adjective + ものを
en.notes: Expresses regret over a missed opportunity or a bad decision.
examples[].german: If only you had told me sooner (but you didn't).
If I had apologized, I would have been forgiven, but I was stubborn and lost out.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ます cannot be attached directly to もの.
ます cannot be attached to the particle を.
This exclamatory expression does not take な.

en.explanation: Expresses that something has a certain quality or leaves an impression that is hard to describe. Often used for emotional or aesthetic impressions.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + ものがある
い-adjective + ものがある
en.notes: Expresses a subjective, often positive impression.
examples[].german: There is something about his playing that touches the heart.
There is something about this painting that makes you think.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ある needs が here, not を.
ます needs the stem あり.
This negates the moving quality.

en.meaning: if one could, if it were possible
en.explanation: Expresses a strong wish, often implying that it is difficult or impossible. Also used for hypothetical negative consequences.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + ものなら
できる + ものなら
en.notes: Can express a wish or a warning, depending on context.
examples[].german: If I could, I'd like to do it over.
If you were to lie, you wouldn't get away with it.
If I could go back, I'd like to return to my student days.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The noun-based condition does not need an extra だ.
を cannot come before the condition here.
ます cannot attach directly to もの.

en.meaning: on the assumption that, as if
en.explanation: Expresses that you take something as given or true and act accordingly. Often in formal or official contexts.
en.formation:
普通形 + ものとして
Noun + (である) + ものとして
en.notes: Often used in business or formal situations.
examples[].german: Let's go ahead with the plan on the assumption that he won't come.
We will treat this matter as resolved.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The dictionary form does not form an assumption link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.
The assumption expression requires と.

en.explanation: Expresses that something looks or feels as if it is about to happen. This structure is used to describe an intense or extreme situation vividly. Emphasizes the immediacy or intensity of a state.
en.formation: Verb ない-stem + んばかりに (する→せんばかりに) / Verb た-form + ばかりに
en.notes: Literary and vivid. する becomes せんばかりに.
examples[].german: He had a look on his face as if he were about to cry at any moment.
The crowd was so full of joy it seemed about to overflow.
He had a look on his face as if he were about to burst into tears at any moment.
He was so happy he practically jumped for joy.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial form does not modify 顔 attributively here.
を cannot connect attributively to 顔 here.
ます cannot be attached directly to ばかり.

en.explanation: Very formal version of ために that expresses a purpose or intention. This archaic structure is used mainly in literary or very formal contexts. Emphasizes the seriousness or importance of the goal.
en.formation: Verb ない-stem + んがために (する→せんがために)
en.notes: Very formal and archaic. する becomes せんがために. Literary style.
examples[].german: He sacrificed everything in order to succeed.
She continued the investigation in order to learn the truth.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The purpose link is completed with に.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to ため.

en.meaning: in the state of ..., as always, typical of ..., despite ...
en.explanation: Expresses that something keeps its original or characteristic state. Used to emphasize that something is in its natural or customary state. Can also express a contrast or an unexpected combination.
en.formation:
名詞 + ながらの + 名詞
イ形容詞 + ながらの + 名詞
動詞辞書形 + ながらの + 名詞
en.notes: Used to emphasize the original or characteristic state. Often used with time references such as 昔 (the old days).
examples[].german: One's true self as it is, a talent one is born with.
It is made using the traditional method.
She has the fresh perspective typical of a student.
He has a natural-born talent.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を cannot link to 才能 as a modifier here.
ます cannot attach directly to ながら.
No extra な comes after の before 才能.

en.explanation: Alternative form of ずにはおかない that expresses the same meaning of inevitability. This form is somewhat less formal, but still elevated language. Used to emphasize that something will inevitably happen.
en.formation: Verb ない-form + ではおかない
en.notes: Synonym of ずにはおかない. The two forms are interchangeable.
examples[].german: This fact is bound to cause an uproar among the public.
Her beauty cannot fail to captivate people.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: Alternative form of ずにはすまない with an identical meaning. Expresses that something has to be done in order to resolve a situation or take responsibility. This form is somewhat more common in modern language than the ず form.
en.formation: Verb ない-form + ではすまない
en.notes: Synonym of ずにはすまない. The two forms are interchangeable.
examples[].german: This problem absolutely has to be explained.
As the person in charge, there will probably be no way around resigning.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This would claim that one could get by without an explanation.
ない does not take an attached ます.
This fixed combination requires で.

en.explanation: You concede that a high degree is not reached, but expect at least a lower one. The second part often contains せめて or 少なくとも, or a recommendation (～べきだ, ～たほうがいい).
en.formation: Verb (ない-form) + までも
en.notes: Often as ～とは言わないまでも ("I won't go as far as to say ..., but"). Despite the similar form, it has a different meaning from ～までもない (N1, "not necessary").
examples[].german: Even if not every day, you should exercise at least once a week.
Even if we can't win, we at least want to make it to the final.
Even if he won't apologize, he should at least explain.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ないばかりか intensifies ("not only not ...") instead of conceding.
からには gives grounds for an obligation and concedes nothing.
ないことには ("unless ...") requires a negative result in the second part.

en.explanation: A double negative expressing that something is possible, albeit with reservations. There is a certain possibility or willingness.
en.formation: Verb ない-form + ものでもない
en.notes: Expresses reserved agreement or a reserved possibility.
examples[].german: If I'm asked, it's not as if I wouldn't help.
Depending on the conditions, it's not out of the question that I'll consider it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
This expression requires the nominal connection でも.

en.meaning: it's not impossible that; it could be that
en.explanation: A double negative expressing that something is possible, even if it seems unlikely. Leaves room for possibility.
en.formation: Verb ない-form + とも限らない
en.notes: Expresses cautious possibility or a warning.
examples[].german: It's not impossible that he'll come.
We might fail, so we need to be careful.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません does not attach to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: Expresses a weak affirmation by using a double negative. This structure means that something is possible, but with reservations or only to a small degree. Used to express cautious or reserved agreement.
en.formation: い-adjective-く + もない / Verb ない-form + くもない / Noun + でなくもない
en.notes: Expresses reserved or cautious agreement. Weaker than a direct affirmation.
examples[].german: What he says is not entirely incomprehensible.
It's not impossible for me to accept that proposal.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
The attributive な-form does not end the sentence here.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is an indispensable condition. Without this condition, the result cannot be achieved.
en.formation:
Noun + なくして(は)
Verb ない-form (く) + なくして(は)
en.notes: A formal expression, often used in speeches or written language.
examples[].german: Without effort there is no success.
Without trust, you can't build a good relationship.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The dictionary form does not form a negative link expressing an accompanying circumstance here.
The finite form does not form a link here.
な cannot be attached here.

en.explanation: ならでは expresses that something is characteristic of, or only possible for, a particular person, place or thing. It stresses uniqueness or distinctiveness. This construction is often used to highlight positive, unique qualities.
en.formation: Noun + ならでは (+ の + Noun)
en.notes: Positive connotation. Stresses uniqueness and special qualities.
examples[].german: This is a dish you can only find in Kyoto.
That's an idea only he could come up with.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The following の connection does not allow an extra な.
を does not fit before の料理 here.
ます cannot be attached to ならでは.

en.meaning: if it were ..., that might be one thing, but
en.explanation: Concedes that something would be understandable in one case, but expresses that it is not acceptable or understandable in the present case.
en.formation:
Noun + ならいざしらず
普通形 + ならいざしらず
en.notes: Expresses a strong contrast between two situations.
examples[].german: If it were a child, that would be one thing, but for an adult to do something like that!
In the old days that might have been fine, but in this day and age it won't work.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a contrastive link here.
ます cannot be attached to ず.

en.meaning: if it were ..., it would still be understandable, but
en.explanation: Concedes that something would be understandable or acceptable in one case, but expresses that this does not apply to the case at hand.
en.formation:
Noun + ならまだしも
普通形 + ならまだしも
en.notes: Expresses a contrast with mild criticism.
examples[].german: If it were a young person, it would be understandable, but for an adult to do something like that!
Once would be understandable, but making the same mistake again and again is a problem.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a contrastive link here.
ます cannot attach to も.

en.explanation: Expresses that one action follows immediately after another. Often with a surprising or unexpected result.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + なり
Verb た-form + なり
en.notes: More literary than やいなや; emphasizes immediacy.
examples[].german: As soon as I got home, I collapsed onto the bed.
The moment he entered the conference room, he started shouting.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: る cannot be attached to ます.
な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a time link here.

en.explanation: Gives examples or alternatives that serve as possibilities. The speaker suggests choosing one of several options.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + なり + Verb 辞書形 + なり
Noun + なり + Noun + なり
en.notes: Expresses that there are several equally valid options.
examples[].german: Please get in touch, whether by phone or by email.
I passed the time reading books or listening to music.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a link for alternatives here.
な cannot be attached here.
る cannot be attached to ます.

en.meaning: at least; even if only (a little)
en.explanation: After expressions for a small amount (少し, 一目, 多少, わずか), なりとも means "even if it is only ...". Written in style and polite; often in requests and wishes.
en.formation: Noun / quantity + なりとも
en.notes: Formulaic in 多少なりとも and 少しなりとも. Same meaning but more everyday: ～でも (少しでも). Do not confuse with ～たりとも～ない ("not even ...") or ～なり～なり ("either ... or").
examples[].german: I would be glad if I could be of even a little help to you.
I want to see them, even if only for a moment.
We are looking for people with at least some experience.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: たりとも goes with a negative ("not in the least") and does not fit a wish.
ばかりか ("not only ... but also") makes no sense here.
ずくめ ("consisting only of") cannot follow 少し.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is not possible without a particular condition or element. This structure emphasizes the necessity or indispensability of something. Often used in formal or emphatic contexts.
en.formation: Noun + なしに/なくして / Verb 辞書形 + ことなしに
en.notes: なくして is more emphatic than なしに. Both emphasize indispensability.
examples[].german: Without effort there is no success.
Without peace, development is impossible.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a link expressing an accompanying circumstance here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to なし.

en.explanation: にあたらない expresses that something is not worth doing, or that there is no reason to behave in a certain way. It is often used to say that a worry, fear or effort is unnecessary. This construction is formal.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + にあたらない / Noun + にあたらない
en.notes: Formal. Used to express that an action or emotion is unnecessary.
examples[].german: Something like that is nothing to be surprised about.
There is no need to worry. It will be resolved soon.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: にあって expresses that something happens in a special or extraordinary situation. It is used to highlight the context or circumstances in which something takes place. This construction is very formal and is used mainly in written language.
en.formation: Noun + にあって
en.notes: Very formal. Used for extraordinary or special situations.
examples[].german: Even in difficult circumstances, one does not lose hope.
In a crisis like this, unity is essential.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: Before も, this concession uses the て-form.
Before も, the て-form is used here.
The finite form does not fit before も here.

en.explanation: にひきかえ is used to highlight a strong contrast between two things. It expresses that, in contrast to one thing, another is very different. It often expresses a negative judgment or disappointment about the contrast.
en.formation: Noun/Sentence + にひきかえ
en.notes: Often has a negative connotation. Stresses an undesirable contrast.
examples[].german: In contrast to the older brother, who is conscientious, the younger brother is lazy.
In contrast to last year's good results, this year has been sluggish.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The point of comparison requires に here.
ます is not attached to the dictionary form.
な does not link the contrast here.

en.explanation: Expresses that a situation has reached a certain point or state, often after a long process. This formal structure is used to describe reaching an end point or conclusion. Can be used for both positive and negative developments.
en.formation: Noun + に至る / Verb 辞書形 + に至る
en.notes: Formal. Emphasizes the process leading up to a certain state.
examples[].german: After many years of research, success was finally achieved.
The situation has reached its worst point.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This negates that success was reached.
The polite past requires the stem 至り.
The plain past is 至った.

en.explanation: Used to highlight an extreme case or a particularly notable example. This structure emphasizes that the example mentioned is especially striking or extreme compared with others. Often followed by a surprising or extreme statement.
en.formation: Noun + に至っては
en.notes: Highlights an extreme or notable case. Often used with negative examples.
examples[].german: Young people these days don't read books. As for him, he doesn't even read manga.
This summer is hot. Last week, it even went above 40 degrees.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: は does not attach to the dictionary form here.
は does not attach to the polite form here.
The highlighted case requires に.

en.explanation: にかぎったことではない expresses that something is not limited to one particular case, person or situation, but applies more generally. It is used to show that a problem or characteristic is more widespread than first assumed.
en.formation: Noun + にかぎったことではない
en.notes: Used to show that something applies more generally than assumed.
examples[].german: This problem is not limited to Japan.
It's not limited to young people, but manners have been getting worse lately.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This would confirm that it is limited to Japan.
ない does not take an attached ます.
Negating a noun requires ではない.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is easy to imagine, understand or predict. This formal structure is used to say that one can easily imagine something. Used mainly in written language.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + にかたくない (推察、想像、理解 etc.)
en.notes: Formal and literary. Mostly used with 想像、推察、予測 etc.
examples[].german: His feelings are not hard to imagine.
That result is not hard to predict.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
This expression links the act of imagining with に.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is the best option or the most ideal state. This structure is used to express a recommendation or preference. Literally means 'there is nothing that goes beyond it'.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/ない-form + に越したことはない / い-adjective + に越したことはない
en.notes: Expresses that something is the best or most ideal option.
examples[].german: Health comes first. Nothing is better than not getting sick.
For safety's sake, it's best to go home early.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ない does not need an object particle here.
The plain past of 越す is 越した.

en.explanation: にもまして expresses that something is even more or stronger than another state or point of comparison. It is used to stress an increase or a surpassing. This expression is formal and often used in written language.
en.formation: Noun + にもまして
en.notes: Formal. Stresses an increase or a surpassing in a comparison.
examples[].german: This year's summer was even hotter than last year's.
She works harder than anyone else.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The finite past form does not form a comparative connection here.
The て-form of 増す is 増して.
な cannot be attached here.

en.explanation: Expresses that something happens before an important event. This formal structure is used to express temporal priority or preparation. Often used in official announcements or formal contexts.
en.formation: Noun + に先立って/に先立ち / Verb 辞書形 + に先立って/に先立ち
en.notes: Formal. に先立って and に先立ち are interchangeable, with に先立ち being somewhat more formal.
examples[].german: Prior to the opening ceremony, a rehearsal was held.
Prior to the launch of the new product, we will hold a press conference.
Before the release, samples were distributed.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The time reference requires に.
The attributive past does not form a link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.

en.meaning: only at/with; and at the same time
en.explanation: にして has several meanings: 1) It expresses that something is only reached at a certain point or level. 2) It can also mean that someone or something has two qualities or roles at the same time. This construction is very formal and literary.
en.formation: Noun + にして
en.notes: Very formal and literary. Has different nuances depending on context.
examples[].german: He is a writer and at the same time also a painter.
Only at the age of 50 did he achieve success for the first time.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The dictionary form does not connect with 画家でもある here.
The finite form does not form a listing connection here.
The attributive past form does not form a listing connection here.

en.explanation: Expresses that something conforms to a rule, a principle or reality. This formal structure is used to emphasize conformity or appropriateness. Common in academic or business contexts.
en.formation: Noun + に即する/に即して/に即した
en.notes: Formal. Used in business, legal or academic contexts.
examples[].german: It is necessary to draw up measures that match the actual situation.
Judgments should be made in accordance with the law.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The stem form cannot modify 対策 attributively here.
る cannot be attached to ます.
The standard being followed requires に.

en.meaning: in accordance with, in line with
en.explanation: にそくして/に即して expresses that something is done in accordance with certain rules, principles or reality. It stresses that one strictly follows or adheres to something. This expression is formal and is often used in business or academic contexts.
en.formation: Noun + にそくして/に即して
en.notes: Formal. Stresses strict conformity with rules or reality.
examples[].german: We need to make plans that are grounded in reality.
Please handle this in accordance with the regulations.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The standard of reference requires に.
The attributive form does not fit before 計画を立てる here.
The finite form does not form a connection here.

en.explanation: Has two meanings: 1) a feeling is so strong that one cannot hold it back; 2) something is unbearable or unworthy. This formal structure is interpreted differently depending on the context. With emotion nouns it often means 'cannot hold back'.
en.formation: Emotion noun + に堪えない / Verb 辞書形 + に堪えない
en.notes: Two meanings: 1) cannot hold back a feeling, 2) to be unbearable.
examples[].german: His death fills me with unbearable sadness.
This sight is unbearable to look at.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
This fixed emotional expression requires に.

en.explanation: にたえる has two opposite meanings: 1) In the positive form it means that something is worth it (鑑賞に堪える = worth viewing). 2) In the negative form (にたえない) it means that something is unbearable or that one cannot bear something. The context determines the meaning.
en.formation: Noun + にたえる/にたえない
en.notes: Very formal. The meaning depends heavily on context (positive vs. negative).
examples[].german: This work is a masterpiece worthy of appreciation.
This pain is unbearable.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The stem form cannot modify 名作 attributively here.
ます is not attached to the dictionary form.
This denies that the work is worth viewing.

en.explanation: に足る expresses that something is worth doing or worthy of being done or received. It emphasizes the value or quality of something. In the negative form (に足りない) it means that something is not worth it or not worthy. This construction is very formal.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/Noun + に足る
en.notes: Very formal. Emphasizes value or worthiness.
examples[].german: This film is a work worth seeing.
He is a person worthy of trust.
This is trustworthy information.
His achievements are praiseworthy.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The stem form cannot modify 作品 attributively here.
ます is not attached to the dictionary form.
This negates that it is worth watching.

en.explanation: Expresses that an action or behavior is inappropriate or unworthy for a particular position or role. A very formal and critical expression.
en.formation: Noun + にあるまじき + Noun
en.notes: Very formal; often used in criticism or official statements.
examples[].german: That is behavior unworthy of a teacher.
He made a remark inappropriate for a doctor.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial form cannot modify 行為 attributively here.
No additional な comes before 行為 here.
ます cannot be attached directly to まじき.

en.explanation: Expresses that someone or something is worthy and lives up to expectations or a reputation. A positive expression.
en.formation: Noun + に恥じない
en.notes: A positive expression that emphasizes worthiness.
examples[].german: He performed in a way worthy of that title.
It was a fight worthy of the name of champion.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
No extra な comes before 活躍 here.
を makes the title the object of being ashamed instead of the standard for a worthy performance.

en.meaning: if you ask ..., in the opinion of
en.explanation: Introduces the opinion or perspective of a particular person. Emphasizes that this is that person's subjective view.
en.formation:
Person + に言わせれば
Person + に言わせると
en.notes: Can be used to distance oneself from the opinion expressed.
examples[].german: If you ask the experts, this is apparently dangerous.
According to her, it's apparently my fault.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The conditional is 言わせれば.
The person whose judgment is given requires に here.
The conditional is not formed with ますば.

en.explanation: Expresses that someone uses a pretext or excuse to do something they actually want to do. The reason given is not the real reason.
en.formation:
Noun + にかこつけて
Verb 辞書形/た-form + のにかこつけて
en.notes: Often has a negative connotation, implying dishonesty.
examples[].german: Under the pretext of work, I went to see her.
Under the pretext of feeling unwell, I skipped the meeting.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: In this expression the pretext requires に.
The attributive past does not form a link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.

en.meaning: to be distracted by, to be absorbed in
en.explanation: Expresses that one is so busy with something that one neglects other important things. Has a negative connotation.
en.formation: Noun + にかまけて
en.notes: Implies criticism of or regret about the neglect.
examples[].german: I got caught up in having fun and neglected my studies.
I was so wrapped up in work that I didn't spend time with my family.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The thing one is occupied with requires に.
The attributive past does not form a link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is unusual or atypical for a person or group. Emphasizes how exceptional it is.
en.formation: Noun + にない + Noun
en.notes: Emphasizes the contrast with normal behavior or the normal state.
examples[].german: It was an unusually serious expression for him.
She showed a kindness that was untypical of her.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
No additional な comes before 真剣な here.
ない does not require an object particle here.

en.meaning: there is no need, not necessary
en.explanation: Expresses that something is not necessary or that one does not have to do something. Often used to reassure someone or dispel concerns.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + には及ばない
Noun + には及ばない
en.notes: A formal expression, often used in polite contexts.
examples[].german: There's no need to worry.
There is no need for an apology.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: Expresses that even under the assumed condition, the result would be no different. Emphasizes that the condition makes no difference.
en.formation:
Noun + にしたところで/にしたって
普通形 + にしたところで
en.notes: Emphasizes the futility or unchangeability of the result.
examples[].german: Even he probably couldn't solve this problem.
Even if we leave now, we won't make it in time.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を and で cannot be combined like this here.
な does not form a concessive link here.
ます cannot attach directly to ところ.

en.explanation: Emphasizes that something only becomes possible or apparent after a certain event or under certain circumstances. Underlines the importance of the precondition.
en.formation:
Noun + にして初めて
Verb て-form + にして初めて
en.notes: Emphasizes the turning point or the decisive realization.
examples[].german: Only through failure did I understand how important it was.
Only when I became a parent could I understand how my parents felt.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The finite past does not form a link here.
The finite polite form does not form a link here.
The connection requires the て-form.

en.explanation: Emphasizes that something applies even in an unexpected or extreme case. Stronger than a simple 'さえ'.
en.formation: Noun + にすら
en.notes: More literary and formal than さえ or でさえ.
examples[].german: He didn't tell the truth even to his parents.
Even experts can't solve this problem.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を cannot follow the recipient marker here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached to すら.

en.explanation: の至り expresses the height or extreme of a feeling or state. It is used mainly with positive emotions such as honor, joy or gratitude, but can also appear with negative emotions. This construction is very formal and polite.
en.formation: Noun + の至り
en.notes: Very formal and polite. Used mainly in formal speeches.
examples[].german: It is the greatest honor to receive an award like this.
I am deeply sorry to have caused you all such worry.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The finite verb form does not fit before です here.
This intensifying expression links the noun with の.
There is no な before です here.

en.explanation: の極み expresses the absolute height or extreme of a feeling or state. It is used with both positive and negative emotions and emphasizes intensity. This construction is very formal and literary.
en.formation: Noun + の極み
en.notes: Very formal and literary. Emphasizes the extreme intensity of a feeling.
examples[].german: His behavior is the height of rudeness.
To receive such an honor is the height of joy.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This intensifying expression links the noun with の.
ます cannot be attached directly to 極み.
There is no な before だ here.

en.explanation: のみならず is a formal expression meaning "not only". It is used to express that something goes beyond the point mentioned and includes additional aspects. This construction is used mainly in formal written language.
en.formation: Noun/Verb-辞書形/い-adjective + のみならず
en.notes: Very formal. Used mainly in written language.
examples[].german: He can speak not only Japanese but also Chinese.
This product is not only of good quality but also reasonably priced.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached to this connection here.
を does not form an additive connection here.
ます cannot be attached to ず.

en.explanation: Expresses that a situation leads to a regrettable or negative outcome. This structure emphasizes that things have become so bad that an undesirable result has occurred. Used only for negative situations.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/た-form + 始末だ
en.notes: Exclusively for negative situations. Expresses regret or criticism.
examples[].german: My debts kept growing, and now it has come to selling the house.
He was constantly late, and in the end it came to him being fired.
I spent too much money and ended up even having to borrow.
He was always late and in the end even got fired.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The object particle does not complete the statement.
The attributive form does not end the sentence.
ます cannot be attached directly to 始末.

en.meaning: no sooner ... than again; as soon as ... right away again
en.explanation: Expresses that immediately after something has been done, the opposite or something negative happens. Emphasizes futility.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/た-form + そばから
en.notes: Often expresses frustration about repeated negative events.
examples[].german: No sooner have I cleaned up than they make a mess again.
As soon as I learn something, I forget it again.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a temporal link here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot attach directly to から.

en.explanation: Expresses that one missed the opportunity to do something even though one intended to. This structure emphasizes that one did not do something because the right moment had passed. Often associated with a feeling of regret.
en.formation: Verb ます-stem + そびれる
en.notes: Often implies regret over the missed opportunity.
examples[].german: There was something I wanted to ask, but I missed my chance.
I missed my chance to eat breakfast, so I'm hungry.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: しまった requires the て-connection.
しまった requires the て-connection.
The finite polite form does not fit before しまった.

en.explanation: Emphasizes that something applies even in an unexpected case. More literary and formal than さえ.
en.formation: Noun + すら
en.notes: Literary style, often used in written language.
examples[].german: He doesn't even remember the name.
It was a situation where you couldn't even drink water.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This particle combination does not connect to 覚えていない here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to すら.

en.explanation: たりとも～ない is a very emphatic negation stressing that not even the smallest amount or number is acceptable. It is often used with words such as 一人、一つ、一日 and has a formal, literary tone.
en.formation: Counter + たりとも + negation
en.notes: Very formal and emphatic. Used mainly in written or formal language.
examples[].german: I can't take even a single day off.
We can't let even a single person slip past us.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not express emphasis on a minimal amount here.
な does not connect with 休むことはできない here.
The copula does not form a connection here.

en.explanation: Expresses a person's status or position. Used to emphasize the duties or expectations associated with that position.
en.formation: Noun + たる + Noun
en.notes: Very formal; often used in moral or philosophical statements.
examples[].german: Anyone who is a teacher must be a role model for their students.
Anyone who is a leader should take responsibility.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: る cannot be attached to ます.
No additional な comes before 者 here.
を cannot connect attributively to 者 here.

en.explanation: Emphatically highlights a particular topic, often followed by an extreme description or evaluation. A very literary expression.
en.formation: Noun + たるや
en.notes: Very literary and formal; not used in modern colloquial speech.
examples[].german: As for its beauty, it is beyond words.
As for his negligence, it is beyond what can be tolerated.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a topic link here.
ます cannot be attached directly to たるや.

en.meaning: even after that still, still nevertheless
en.explanation: Expresses that even after something has been done or has happened, a state or situation continues to exist. This structure emphasizes the persistence or stubbornness of a state despite previous actions. Used to express surprise or admiration.
en.formation: Verb て-form + なお
en.notes: Emphasizes the continuation of a state despite counteracting factors.
examples[].german: Even after failing many times, he still did not give up.
Even after hearing the explanation, I still can't understand it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This connecting expression requires the て-form.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to なお.

en.explanation: Expresses that something would be natural, appropriate or expected. This formal structure is used to say that something should be as reason or morality demands. Often used in critical or evaluative contexts.
en.formation: Verb て-form + 然るべき + Noun
en.notes: Very formal and literary. 然る (しかる) means 'to be so, to be appropriate'.
examples[].german: The government ought to give a proper explanation of this problem.
As the person responsible, he is in a position where he ought to apologize.
Problems like this should naturally be dealt with promptly.
It would only be right to thank him.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This expression requires the て-connection.
The adverbial form does not fit before だ here.
No additional な comes before だ here.

en.explanation: Expresses that someone says or does something without restraint or shame. This structure is often used to describe excessive self-confidence or brazenness. It can have a positive (bold) or negative (presumptuous) connotation.
en.formation: Verb て-form + はばからない
en.notes: Can be admiring or critical, depending on the context. Emphasizes a lack of restraint.
examples[].german: He doesn't hesitate to say that he's the best.
She doesn't shy away from stating her opinion openly.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The connection after 言っ requires the て-form.
ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.

en.explanation: Expresses that a situation is so unpleasant or burdensome that one cannot stand it. This structure is used to express strong dissatisfaction or complaints. Emphasizes how unbearable a state is.
en.formation: Verb て-form + はかなわない / い-adjective-くて + はかなわない
en.notes: Expresses a strong complaint or dissatisfaction about a situation.
examples[].german: The room next door is so noisy it's unbearable.
Being made to work overtime every day is unbearable.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.
The connection after うるさく requires て.

en.explanation: Expresses a deep, unceasing wish or strong feeling that does not let up. This very formal structure is used mainly in written language. Often combined with verbs such as 願う (to wish), 祈る (to pray), 望む (to hope).
en.formation: Verb て-form + やまない
en.notes: Very formal; often used in speeches, greetings or written addresses.
examples[].german: I sincerely wish you all good health and happiness.
I pray unceasingly for world peace.
I never cease to wish for world peace.
I pray fervently for his success.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: After 祈っ, this expression requires the て-form.
ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.

en.meaning: since one has (already) ... (and must save face)
en.explanation: 手前 (literally "in front of oneself") justifies an action out of concern for one's own standing: because you have said or done something, or are in front of others, you have no other choice.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form / た-form) + 手前; Noun + の + 手前
en.notes: The second part usually expresses a compulsion: ～わけにはいかない, ～なければならない, ～しかない. Related: ～以上(は) and ～上は (N2), which give reasons more neutrally. As a noun, 手前 also means "just before, on this side of" (駅の手前).
examples[].german: Since I promised to help, I can't back out now.
In front of their children, parents can't break a promise.
Having said "I'll definitely win", I can't afford to lose.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: くせに ("even though") reproaches others and does not justify a compulsion.
とたん ("the moment that") is purely temporal.
ついでに ("while one is at it") does not fit a compulsion.

en.meaning: it's no problem if, it's fine to
en.explanation: A formal expression that grants permission or consent. Expresses that something is acceptable and causes no problems.
en.formation: Verb て-form + も差し支えない
en.notes: Very formal; often in business or official contexts.
examples[].german: You may take photos here without any problem.
It's fine if you come tomorrow.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません does not attach to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: Expresses that two or more factors work together and produce a particular result. This structure emphasizes that different elements reinforce each other. Used in formal or analytical contexts to describe causes or factors.
en.formation: Noun + と相まって
en.notes: Formal. Emphasizes the interplay of several positive or negative factors.
examples[].german: Coupled with the good weather, sales went up.
His effort together with his talent led to success.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The factor that works together with the other requires と.
The attributive past does not form a link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.

en.meaning: if it is the case that, if it's for
en.explanation: とあれば expresses that if a certain condition or situation arises, one is prepared to do whatever is necessary. It stresses determination or readiness to act under the circumstances mentioned. This construction is often used to express strong motivation or commitment.
en.formation: Noun/の + とあれば
en.notes: Stresses determination or readiness under certain circumstances.
examples[].german: If it's for my child, I'll do anything.
If the company's survival is at stake, we have no choice but to cooperate.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The conditional of ある is あれば.
The assumed statement requires と.
The conditional is not formed with ますば.

en.explanation: とあって expresses that a certain situation or reaction occurs because of a special or extraordinary circumstance. It stresses that the reason mentioned is special or unusual and therefore has a corresponding consequence. This construction is often used to describe special events or circumstances.
en.formation: Noun + とあって / Sentence + とあって
en.notes: Stresses special or extraordinary circumstances as the reason.
examples[].german: Since it was a concert by a famous singer, the venue was packed.
Since it was the first sale of the New Year, crowds of customers gathered from early morning.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive past form does not form a causal connection here.
The finite form does not form a causal connection here.
The expression of reason requires と.

en.explanation: といえども is a very formal way of saying "although" or "even if". It is used to express that even under the circumstances mentioned, or despite a certain quality, something else is the case. This construction has a literary, elevated tone.
en.formation: Noun + といえども / Verb/Adjective + といえども
en.notes: Very formal and literary. Used mainly in written language.
examples[].german: However much of a genius one may be, one cannot succeed without effort.
Even though they are children, their human rights should be respected.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The quoting connection requires と.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached to ども.

en.explanation: といい～といい is used to list several aspects or examples that all share a common evaluation or quality. It stresses that both one and the other apply. This construction is often used to give an overall assessment.
en.formation: Noun + といい + Noun + といい
en.notes: Used to stress several positive (or negative) aspects.
examples[].german: Both in personality and in ability, he is perfect.
Both the scenery and the food in this town are wonderful.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The listing expression uses と.
る cannot be attached to ます.
な does not form a parallel evaluative connection here.

en.explanation: ときたら is used to express criticism or dissatisfaction about someone or something. It highlights a topic one wants to complain about. This construction always has a negative or critical connotation and is used in spoken language.
en.formation: Noun + ときたら
en.notes: Always has a negative or critical connotation. Colloquial.
examples[].german: As for my son, he doesn't study and does nothing but play games.
As for young people these days, they have no manners.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The highlighted topic requires と.
The conditional of 来る is 来たら.
The conditional is not formed with ますたら.

en.explanation: ともあろう is used to express surprise or disappointment that someone with a certain status or position has done something unexpected or inappropriate. It stresses that, because of their position, more would have been expected of that person. This construction often has a critical connotation.
en.formation: Noun + ともあろう (+ 者が/人が/方が)
en.notes: Expresses surprise or criticism. Stresses behavior that is inappropriate for the person's status.
examples[].german: To think that a teacher, of all people, would make such a mistake!
It's unbelievable that someone in the position of company president would break a promise.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No extra な comes before 人 here.
る cannot be attached to ます.
The presumptive form of ある is あろう.

en.meaning: when it comes to; once one reaches the point of
en.explanation: ともなると/ともなれば expresses that at a certain high level, status or stage, special circumstances or expectations apply. It stresses that the situation or status is not ordinary and therefore has special consequences.
en.formation: Noun + ともなると/ともなれば
en.notes: Stresses a special status or level. Often interchangeable with になると, but ともなると is more emphatic.
examples[].german: Once you're a company president, your responsibilities get heavier too.
When you're a professional, daily practice is essential.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a condition here.
ます requires the stem なり.
な cannot be attached to the conditional.

en.meaning: if it is the case that, under these circumstances
en.explanation: Expresses that, under certain special circumstances, a corresponding reaction or action is natural or unavoidable.
en.formation:
普通形 + とあっては
Noun + とあっては
en.notes: Emphasizes the inevitability or naturalness of the reaction.
examples[].german: If it's an order from the company president, I can't refuse.
Under these circumstances, it can't be helped.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: は does not connect to the dictionary form here.
は does not connect to the polite form here.
を does not form a conditional link here.

en.meaning: as if to say, as though
en.explanation: Describes an action or state as if the person were saying or expressing something specific. The actual words are not spoken, but the action conveys this meaning.
en.formation:
普通形 + とばかりに
フレーズ + とばかりに
en.notes: Often used with verbs of movement or with gestures.
examples[].german: He thumped his chest as if to say, 'Leave it to me.'
The children rushed outside as if they had been waiting for this moment.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form an adverbial link here.
な does not connect to 胸をたたいた here.
ます cannot be attached directly to ばかり.

en.explanation: Gives a rough estimate or assessment. Often expresses that something is modest or limited.
en.formation:
Number/amount + といったところだ
普通形 + といったところだ
en.notes: Often expresses a modest or realistic assessment.
examples[].german: There are about 30 participants, I'd say.
His ability is intermediate level at best.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The object particle does not end the sentence.
The attributive form does not end the sentence.
ます cannot attach directly to ところ.

en.explanation: Emphasizes that a state has continued without interruption over a longer period. Often used with time expressions.
en.formation: Time expression + というもの
en.notes: Emphasizes continuity over the entire period.
examples[].german: Ever since then, I haven't seen him at all.
This whole past week, it's been nothing but rain.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The quoting connection requires と.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot attach directly to もの.

en.explanation: Expresses that someone is or was just in the middle of doing something when they were interrupted or something else happened. This structure is often used to express an apology or gratitude. Emphasizes the timing of the interruption.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/ている-form/た-form + ところを
en.notes: Often used in polite apologies or expressions of thanks.
examples[].german: Thank you for taking the time, even though you're busy.
I'm sorry to disturb you while you're resting.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な does not connect the following clause here.
ます cannot be attached directly to ところ.
ます cannot be attached to を.

en.meaning: as soon as one sees/notices that
en.explanation: Expresses that an action follows immediately after noticing or seeing something. Emphasizes the speed of the reaction.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形/た-form + とみるや
en.notes: A literary expression; emphasizes a quick reaction.
examples[].german: As soon as he saw me, he ran off.
As soon as he saw a chance, he took action immediately.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: Classifying what one sees requires と.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot attach directly to や.

en.explanation: A literary expression for "even if" or "even though". Used mainly in formal or literary texts.
en.formation:
Verb 辞書形 + とも
い-adjective + とも
en.notes: Very literary; rare in spoken language.
examples[].german: Even if it rains, I will go.
Even if it is difficult, I will take on the challenge.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a concessive link here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot attach directly to とも.

en.explanation: Expresses that an action is carried out without a clear intention or particular goal. The person acts unconsciously or aimlessly.
en.formation:
Verb ます-form + ともなく/ともなしに
聞く → 聞くともなく
en.notes: Emphasizes the absence of intention or awareness.
examples[].german: I was absent-mindedly watching TV without really paying attention.
I was gazing at the sky without really looking at it.
I kept walking with no particular destination.
For no particular reason, I found myself remembering her.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a link expressing an accompanying circumstance here.

en.meaning: to tend to, to easily end up
en.explanation: Expresses that one easily gets into a certain (usually negative) situation or tends toward a certain behavior. This structure is used to describe a tendency or susceptibility. Often followed by negative consequences or states.
en.formation: ともすれば / ともすると (no conjugation needed)
en.notes: ともすれば and ともすると are interchangeable. Mostly used with negative tendencies.
examples[].german: When you're busy, you easily tend to damage your health.
When you're alone, you easily become pessimistic.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form an adverbial expression of tendency here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます requires the stem し.

en.explanation: Hypothetically assumes that something is the case, and then shows that the result would still be no different.
en.formation:
普通形 + としたところで
Noun + としたところで
en.notes: Emphasizes the futility or unchangeability of the result.
examples[].german: Even if we hurried now, we wouldn't make it in time.
Even if we asked him, he probably wouldn't help us.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を and で cannot be combined like this here.
な does not form a concessive link here.
ます cannot attach directly to ところ.

en.explanation: とて is a literary, archaic form meaning 'even if' or 'even'. It is used to express that even in an extreme case something is not possible or does not hold. This construction is found mainly in literary texts or very formal language.
en.formation: Noun + とて
en.notes: Very literary and archaic. Hardly used in modern colloquial speech.
examples[].german: However rich you may be, that doesn't necessarily mean you're happy.
Even parents cannot know everything about their children.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a concessive link here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached directly to とて.

en.explanation: Expresses surprise, indignation or disbelief about a fact. Also used to define something or explain what something means.
en.formation:
Sentence + とは
フレーズ + とは
en.notes: The 'は' after 'と' emphasizes the statement and often expresses astonishment.
examples[].german: I never thought he would do something like that.
It's a surprise that she's actually quitting.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The content of the thought requires と instead of を.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot be attached to は.

en.explanation: A very literary and archaic expression describing two actions being performed alternately. Used almost exclusively in classical texts.
en.formation: Verb ます-stem + つ + Verb ます-stem + つ
en.notes: Very archaic; hardly used in modern language.
examples[].german: We moved on, going back and forth.
Now crying, now laughing, emotions swung back and forth.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: つ attaches to the verb stems 行き and 戻り.
つ does not attach to the polite form.
The expression uses verb stems, not past forms.

en.explanation: After words for a feeling or impression, ったらない means "so much that it cannot be described". Colloquial; more written: ～といったらない.
en.formation: い-adj (dictionary form) + ったらない; Noun (often ending in ～さ) + といったらない
en.notes: Mostly for negative feelings (怖い, 寂しい, 腹立たしい), less often positive ones (うれしいったらない). Do not confuse with ～ったら (N2), which singles out a person with annoyance. Similar: ～極まりない (N1, written) and ～てしょうがない (N2).
examples[].german: Walking alone on the street at night is incredibly scary.
I fell over on a packed train; it was so embarrassing.
His bragging is unbearably relentless.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 怖いことはない means "there's no need to be afraid", the opposite.
わけがない ("can't possibly ...") denies the feeling instead of intensifying it.
ほどではない ("not that much") weakens instead of intensifying.

en.explanation: はおろか expresses that not even the simpler or more basic thing is possible, let alone the more difficult or advanced one. It is used to stress that not even a lower level is reached. The construction follows the pattern: harder/higher はおろか easier/lower not ... either.
en.formation: Noun + はおろか
en.notes: Stresses that even the simpler thing is not possible. The harder thing is mentioned first.
examples[].german: He can't even read hiragana, let alone kanji.
I'm so busy that I don't even have time to see a movie, let alone travel.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form an escalating connection here.
ます cannot be attached directly to おろか.
The attributive form does not connect to ひらがなも読めない here.

en.explanation: Expresses that something is obvious or self-evident and does not need to be mentioned specifically. Then emphasizes additional examples.
en.formation: Noun + は言うに及ばず
en.notes: A very formal expression, often found in written language.
examples[].german: He can speak French, not to mention English.
It is popular in the regions too, not to mention Tokyo.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached here.
を does not form an additive link here.
ます cannot attach to ず.

en.explanation: Temporarily sets a topic aside in order to talk about something else. Signals a change of topic.
en.formation: Noun + はさておき/はさておいて
en.notes: Useful for changing the topic or setting priorities.
examples[].german: Joking aside, let's get to the main topic.
Leaving money aside, let's make a plan first.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive past does not form a link here.
The finite form does not form a link here.
な cannot be attached here.

en.explanation: を踏まえて expresses that one does something taking into account, or on the basis of, certain information, experiences or circumstances. It stresses that one incorporates the factors mentioned into one's considerations or actions. This construction is often used in formal or business contexts.
en.formation: Noun + を踏まえて
en.notes: Formal. Used in business and official contexts.
examples[].german: Based on past experience, we drew up a new plan.
Based on the survey results, we will consider countermeasures.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive form does not connect the following clause here.
The finite form does not form a connection here.
The basis taken into account requires を.

en.explanation: を経て expresses that something has gone through a particular process, period or series of stages. It stresses the course or development over time or space. This construction is often used to describe historical developments, career paths or journeys.
en.formation: Noun + を経て
en.notes: Stresses the process or development over time. Formal.
examples[].german: After long discussions, we finally reached an agreement.
After going through various jobs, he arrived at his current position.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive form does not connect the following clause here.
The finite form does not form a connection here.
The stage gone through requires を.

en.explanation: を限りに expresses that something ends at a certain point in time and does not continue afterward. It marks a clear end point or conclusion. This construction is often used in official announcements to proclaim the end of something.
en.formation: Point in time/Noun + を限りに
en.notes: Used for official announcements that something is ending. Marks a clear end point.
examples[].german: As of today, I'm quitting smoking.
This store will close at the end of this month.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The time limit connects with に.
The fixed expression requires を at the beginning.
な does not form a temporal connection here.

en.explanation: を皮切りに expresses that something is the starting point or beginning of a series of events or activities. It is used to show that further events follow after the first. This construction is often used in the context of tours, event series or developments.
en.formation: Noun + を皮切りに
en.notes: Often used for tours, event series or developments.
examples[].german: Starting in Tokyo, we'll hold a nationwide tour.
Starting with this incident, various problems came to light.
Beginning with this incident, various problems became apparent.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The expression connects with に.
The starting point requires を.
ます cannot be attached directly to 皮切り.

en.explanation: Expresses that one cannot suppress a strong feeling. This formal structure is used to describe involuntary emotional reactions. Used mainly with emotion words such as 感動 (being moved), 驚き (surprise), 怒り (anger).
en.formation: Emotion noun + を禁じ得ない
en.notes: Very formal. Used mainly with nouns of emotion.
examples[].german: I cannot help being moved by his courage.
I cannot help being surprised by this result.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
The feeling that cannot be suppressed requires を.

en.explanation: をものともせずに expresses that someone acts resolutely despite difficulties, obstacles or adverse circumstances, without letting them have any effect. It stresses strong will and the determination not to be held back by problems. This construction often has an admiring connotation.
en.formation: Noun + をものともせずに
en.notes: Stresses determination and strong will. Often with an admiring connotation.
examples[].german: Undaunted by the difficulties, he kept taking on challenges.
They set off in defiance of the storm.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form an adverbial connection here.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.
な cannot be attached here.

en.explanation: Expresses that even with a particular means or under a particular condition, something cannot be achieved. This formal structure emphasizes that a normally effective means is not enough in this case. Used to underline the difficulty or impossibility of something.
en.formation: Noun + をもってしても
en.notes: Very formal. Emphasizes that something is not possible despite a powerful means.
examples[].german: Even with modern science, this disease cannot be cured.
Even with his efforts, winning the championship will probably be difficult.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The concessive link requires しても.
も does not attach to the polite form here.
を does not form a concessive link here.

en.meaning: there is nothing/no one other than
en.explanation: をおいてほかにない emphatically expresses that there is no choice or alternative other than the person or thing mentioned. It stresses that only this one option comes into question. This expression is very formal and is often used to stress the absolute suitability or necessity of something.
en.formation: Noun + をおいてほかにない
en.notes: Very emphatic. Stresses uniqueness or absolute suitability.
examples[].german: There is no one but him for this job.
No one but you can solve this problem now.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This asserts that there are other possibilities instead of exclusivity.
ない does not take an attached ます.
ない does not require an object particle here.

en.explanation: を余儀なくされる expresses that one is forced by external circumstances or necessity to do something one does not actually want to do. It stresses that there is no choice and that one has to act against one's will. This construction is often used in formal or official contexts.
en.formation: Noun + を余儀なくされる
en.notes: Formal. Stresses reluctant necessity due to external circumstances.
examples[].german: Because of the typhoon, we were forced to cancel the event.
Due to financial difficulties, we were forced to close the factory.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The polite past requires the verb stem.
The negative endings cannot be combined like this.
ます cannot be attached to the plain past form.

en.explanation: Expresses that external circumstances force someone to do something. This formal structure emphasizes that there is no other choice. Often used in news or formal reports to describe involuntary actions.
en.formation: Noun + を余儀なくさせる / Verb 辞書形 + ことを余儀なくさせる
en.notes: Formal. Active form of を余儀なくされる. Emphasizes external compulsion.
examples[].german: The typhoon forced many people to evacuate.
The recession is forcing the company to cut staff.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The polite past requires the verb stem.
ます cannot be attached to the plain past.
The negative endings cannot be combined like this.

en.explanation: をよそに expresses that someone does something without regard for the feelings, expectations or situation of others. It stresses that the action runs counter to what is expected or wished. This construction often has a critical or negative connotation.
en.formation: Noun + をよそに
en.notes: Often with a critical or negative connotation. Stresses a lack of consideration.
examples[].german: Ignoring his parents' worries, he keeps doing dangerous work.
Ignoring the opposition of those around her, she carried out her plan.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The expression connects with に.
な does not form an adverbial connection here.
ます cannot be attached to よそ.

en.explanation: A very literary expression meaning "as soon as" or "no sooner ... than". Used almost exclusively in written language.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + や
en.notes: Very literary and archaic; rare in modern language.
examples[].german: The moment he saw me, he ran off.
As soon as she heard the news, she started to cry.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a temporal link here.
な cannot be attached here.
ます cannot attach directly to や.

en.meaning: no sooner than, as soon as
en.explanation: Expresses that one action follows immediately after another. This formal structure emphasizes the immediacy and speed of the consecutive events. Used mainly in written language.
en.formation: Verb 辞書形 + や否や
en.notes: Formal and literary. Emphasizes the immediate succession of two events.
examples[].german: No sooner had I got home than the phone rang.
As soon as the exam was over, the students rushed out of the classroom.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: な cannot be attached here.
を does not form a time link here.
ます cannot be attached directly to や否や.

en.explanation: Expresses that no matter what happens or is done, the result stays the same. This structure is used to emphasize that something holds under all circumstances. Often used in the form AようがBようが.
en.formation: Verb 意向形 + が/と / Verb 意向形 + が + Verb 意向形 + が
en.notes: ようが and ようと are interchangeable. Often in the form AようがBようが.
examples[].german: Whether it rains or not, the match will be held.
Whatever you do, the result won't change.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The concessive volitional form does not combine with を.
ます cannot be attached to the volitional form.
な cannot be attached here.

en.meaning: even if one wanted to, one can't
en.explanation: Expresses that one would like to do something but cannot for objective reasons. This structure emphasizes impossibility despite the wish or intention. Used to express frustration or helplessness.
en.formation: Verb 意向形 + にも + Verb 可能形-ない
en.notes: Emphasizes impossibility despite the wish or intention.
examples[].german: I have no money, so even if I wanted to buy it, I couldn't.
I don't know the phone number, so I can't get in touch even if I want to.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This affirms that buying is possible.
ない does not take an attached ます.
The volitional form of 買う is 買おう.

en.explanation: Encouragement or a call to a group to do something together. Often in speeches or formal addresses.
en.formation:
Verb 意向形 + ではないか
Verb 意向形 + じゃないか
en.notes: Often used in inspiring speeches or appeals.
examples[].german: Let us all join forces and do our best!
Shall we not seize this opportunity and give it a try?
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The volitional form is 頑張ろう.
ない does not take an attached ます.
ます cannot attach to the question particle.

en.explanation: ゆえに is a very formal and literary way of expressing a reason or cause. It corresponds to English "because of" or "due to" and is used mainly in formal written language. It gives the sentence a serious, elevated tone.
en.formation: Noun + ゆえに / な-adjective-である + ゆえに / い-adjective + ゆえに
en.notes: Very formal and literary. Used mainly in written language.
examples[].german: It was a mistake born of youth.
I failed because of a lack of experience.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a link expressing a reason here.
な does not connect the following clause here.
ます cannot be attached to ゆえ.

en.explanation: Expresses that an action or event will inevitably occur, or that one cannot help doing something. This structure emphasizes the inevitability of an action. Often used to express strong emotions or reactions.
en.formation: Verb ない-stem + ずにはおかない (する→せずにはおかない)
en.notes: Formal and literary. The form with する is せずにはおかない.
examples[].german: This film cannot fail to move those who see it.
His speech could not fail to astonish the audience.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない does not take an attached ます.
ません is not attached to the dictionary form.
The polite past is not formed with ないました.

en.explanation: Expresses that one absolutely must do something in order to set a situation right or live up to one's responsibility. This structure emphasizes moral obligation or social necessity. Often used when one feels guilty or has to make amends.
en.formation: Verb ない-stem + ずにはすまない (する→せずにはすまない)
en.notes: Emphasizes moral or social obligation more strongly than ずにはおかない.
examples[].german: I broke my promise, so I absolutely have to apologize.
I caused him trouble, so I absolutely have to apologize to him.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This would claim that one could get by without apologizing.
ない does not take an attached ます.
This fixed combination requires に.

en.meaning: after a long ..., in the end (with a bad outcome)
en.explanation: あげく describes how a long, often laborious or nerve-racking process ends in a usually negative or unwanted result. Common in storytelling and complaints; intensified as あげくの果てに ("to top it all off").
en.formation: Verb (た-form) + あげく(に) / Noun + の + あげく(に)
en.notes: Unlike ～末に, which can be neutral or even positive (悩んだ末に決めた), あげく is almost always negatively colored and sounds disappointed or annoyed. The main clause describes a result that has already happened; あげく is not suitable for intentions or requests.
examples[].german: After going back and forth for ages, I ended up not buying anything.
After arguing with his boss, he ended up quitting the company.
After a long discussion, the plan was eventually scrapped.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: うちに does not follow the た-form and does not mark an end point after long hesitation.
とたん describes a sudden event immediately afterward and does not fit with 散々 and 結局.
ついでに means "while you're at it" and makes no sense with the disappointing result.

en.meaning: out of too much, out of sheer
en.explanation: あまり expresses that a feeling or state is so extreme that it leads to an (often unusual) result.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form) / verb-た形 + あまり / noun + の + あまり
en.notes: Often used with emotions or intense states.
examples[].german: I cried out of sheer happiness.
I thought about it so much that I couldn't sleep.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not link a cause-and-effect clause here.
な does not connect with 泣いてしまった here.
ます cannot be attached to the noun あまり.

en.explanation: ばかりだ after a verb of change describes a development that keeps going relentlessly in one direction, almost always for the worse: 悪くなるばかりだ. The speaker sounds worried or resigned. Neutral to written; also in news style.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form, verb of change) + ばかりだ
en.notes: Almost synonymous with ～一方だ, but ばかりだ is even more firmly tied to negative developments; 一方だ can also be neutral (利用者は増える一方だ). Don't confuse it with ～ばかり (N4, "only, nothing but"), ～たばかり ("just did") or ～んばかり (N1, "as if about to").
examples[].german: Even though I'm taking medicine, my symptoms just keep getting worse.
This town's population just keeps shrinking.
The talks made no progress, and the conflict between the two countries only kept deepening.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: べきだ expresses an obligation; symptoms are not "supposed" to get worse.
ことはない means "there's no need to" and makes no sense with のに.
つもりだ expresses an intention; symptoms have no will.

en.meaning: to act like, to pretend to be
en.explanation: ぶる forms verbs meaning "to (overly) present oneself as X": 偉ぶる (to act important), 上品ぶる (to act refined), 知ったかぶり (pretending to know). Always pejorative: someone fakes a quality or shows it off. Conjugates like a godan verb.
en.formation: Noun / い-adjective (stem) / な-adjective (stem) + ぶる (ぶって, ぶらない ...)
en.notes: ～がる (N4) describes the feelings or wishes of third persons as they show outwardly (寒がる), without reproach. ～ぶる, by contrast, implies fakeness or showing off. ～っぽい (N4) means "seems like, tends to" and is not necessarily negative.
examples[].german: He's only moved up a little, and he's already putting on airs.
