There's no way anyone could fail to understand such an easy question.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This asserts that there is a reason instead of rejecting the possibility.
ない does not take an attached ます.
The negation needs が here, not を.

en.meaning: first and foremost ..., starting with ... (and others)
en.explanation: をはじめとする names a representative or especially important example and implies a larger group: "X and many others". Attributively before nouns (をはじめとする + Noun), adverbially as をはじめとして. More formal than ～をはじめ; typical of the news, speeches and corporate texts.
en.formation: Noun + をはじめとする / をはじめとした + Noun; Noun + をはじめとして、～
en.notes: ～をはじめ (N3) is the shorter, slightly less formal form with the same meaning. The example named must be typical of or outstanding in the group. Difference from ～を中心に: that describes a spatial or thematic center, not the first member of a list.
examples[].german: In big cities, Tokyo first and foremost, rents keep going up.
Led by the principal, many teachers attended the graduation ceremony.
Japanese food, sushi above all, is very popular abroad too.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: Before a noun, を中心とする would be needed; を中心に is adverbial.
をめぐって ("over, concerning" a dispute) cannot come directly before 大都市.
はじめて means "for the first time" and does not link an example to a noun.

en.explanation: を兼ねて expresses that one action serves several purposes at the same time: "a trip to the bakery that doubles as a walk". Often AとBを兼ねて. Neutral to polite; common in letters, invitations and company events. Attributive: を兼ねた + noun.
en.formation: Noun + を兼ねて / を兼ねた + Noun; Noun A + と + Noun B + を兼ねて
en.notes: ～ついでに (N3) describes a side action that happens to present itself; を兼ねて names a purpose that is intended at the same time. ～がてら (N1) is similar but more literary and mostly used with verbs of motion. Also written をかねて.
examples[].german: I walked to the bakery in front of the station – partly as a stroll.
We held a dinner that served as both a New Year party and a welcome party.
I'm looking for a job that combines my hobby with practical benefit.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: をめぐって requires a dispute or a discussion.
を問わず requires a category (年齢を問わず), not a purpose.
に反して means "contrary to" and makes no sense with the walk.

en.meaning: taking ... as an occasion, as a turning point
en.explanation: を契機に describes an event that served as a turning point or trigger for an important change. More formal than をきっかけに.
en.formation: Noun + を契機に(して) / を契機として
en.notes: More formal than をきっかけに. Often used for social changes.
examples[].german: The earthquake disaster prompted a rise in disaster-preparedness awareness.
He took his marriage as an occasion to rethink his life.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The phrase marking the occasion ends with に.
The starting point needs を here.
契機 does not form a な-connection here.

en.explanation: をめぐって is used when there is a discussion, a dispute or differing opinions about a topic.
en.formation: Noun + をめぐって / をめぐる + noun
en.notes: Always implies disagreement or conflict.
examples[].german: A dispute broke out over ownership of the land.
The debate over this issue continues.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive form does not connect to 争いが起きた here.
The point of dispute takes を here.
The finite form does not link the subject of the dispute here.

en.meaning: based on, on the basis of
en.explanation: をもとに expresses that something serves as the basis, source or starting point for something else. Often used with creative works or decisions.
en.formation: Noun + をもとに(して) / をもとにした + noun
en.notes: Similar to に基づいて, but をもとに is somewhat more casual.
examples[].german: This movie was made based on a true story.
We came up with improvement measures based on the survey results.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The basis is linked to 作られた with に.
The fixed combination is をもとに.
の requires a following noun here.

en.explanation: をもって is used in formal contexts: 1) with a means/method, 2) as of a certain point in time (deadline).
en.formation: Noun + をもって
en.notes: Very formal, often in announcements and business language.
examples[].german: As of today, we will be discontinuing this service.
To respond with sincerity.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The て-form of 持つ is 持って, with a small っ.
The finite form does not form a link marking the end point in time here.
に and を cannot appear together here.

en.explanation: を除いて explicitly excludes one case: "all/always, just not X". More formal than ～以外(は) and common in rules, announcements, weather reports and statistics. Often used with all-inclusive statements such as 全員, 毎日 or with a negative. Attributively: を除く + Noun.
en.formation: Noun + を除いて / を除き / を除く + Noun / を除けば
en.notes: Same meaning as ～以外(は), but more formal. ～を抜きにして (N2) means "without taking X into account / including X" and emphasizes leaving out an element that would normally be needed, not an exception to a rule. を除けば often introduces a qualification: 値段を除けば完璧だ.
examples[].german: We're open every day except Sunday.
Everyone agreed except for one person.
Except for some areas, it will probably be sunny tomorrow.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を問わず is used with a category (曜日を問わず), not with a single day.
に限って singles out one case as "of all times / only" and contradicts 毎日.
をめぐって requires a dispute or discussion, not opening hours.

en.meaning: X as Y (to set, to regard)
en.explanation: を～として/とする specifies what role or function something has: "to take X as Y, to make X the Y" – for example 目標, 目的, 条件, テーマ. Formal; common in rules, plans, reports and the news. Attributive: を～とする / とした + noun.
en.formation: Noun A + を + Noun B + として / とする / とした + Noun
en.notes: Plain ～として (N4) marks a role of the subject (教師として働く). In を～として, by contrast, an object is explicitly declared to be something. ～を中心として and ～をはじめとして are fixed variants of this pattern.
examples[].german: He studies every day with the goal of becoming a Japanese teacher.
The purpose of this event is to revitalize the region.
A lecture on the theme of environmental problems was held.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: について cannot follow ～を目標; the verb that governs を is missing.
に対して cannot attach to an object marked with を.
によって ("by, depending on") cannot attach to an object marked with を.

en.meaning: among other things ... and ...; partly ..., partly ...
en.explanation: やら～やら lists examples from a jumbled set and suggests there was more besides, often with a sense of chaos, stress or mixed emotions (嬉しいやら恥ずかしいやら). Used in speech and writing; more emotional than ～とか～とか.
en.formation: Noun / Verb (dictionary form) / い-adjective + やら, Noun / Verb / い-adjective + やら
en.notes: ～とか～とか is more neutral and more colloquial; ～たり～たり lists actions without an emotional undertone. With やら～やら, by contrast, there is almost always a sense of "it was all too much / all over the place". A single やら after question words (何やら, どこへやら), on the other hand, means "somehow, somewhere".
examples[].german: What with getting ready for the move, work and so on, I'm busy every day.
I was partly happy and partly embarrassed: a mixed feeling.
People were crying and shouting; the hall was in an uproar.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ばかりか requires も or まで in the second part, not a parallel やら.
どころか turns an expectation into its opposite; here, burdens are simply being listed.
につき is a formal reason and cannot be part of a list.

en.explanation: ようでは (colloquially ようじゃ) presents an undesirable behavior or a bad state as a condition and draws a negative result from it: "If you already fail at this, it's hopeless." Critical and admonishing; often used by superiors.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form/ない-form/ている-form) + ようでは / ようじゃ + negative consequence
en.notes: Unlike neutral ～ば/～たら, ようでは contains a judgment: the behavior is criticized as inadequate. The main clause is practically always negative (困る, 無理だ, だめだ). Do not confuse with ～ようではないか (N1, "let's ...") or ～ようで ("it seems, and ...").
examples[].german: If you can't even solve a simple problem like this, passing will be tough.
Someone who's late every morning is a failure as a working adult.
If you're crying over something like that, you won't make it from here on.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ように expresses a purpose or request ("so that") and makes no sense here.
ようがない follows the ます-stem (解きようがない), not the ない-form.
ようでも ("even if it seems so") is concessive and contradicts the conclusion.

en.meaning: depending on how one ...; from a certain angle
en.explanation: ようによっては expresses that a matter can look completely different depending on how one views or approaches it: "Depending on how you look at it, this is actually an opportunity." Mostly with 考える, 見る, やる; the main clause often contains a surprising view.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + ようによっては
en.notes: The noun ～よう (ます-stem + よう) means "way, manner", as in ～ようがない ("there's no way to"). ～によっては (N2) follows ordinary nouns (場合によっては); ようによっては refers specifically to the way of doing or thinking. Same meaning: 考え方によっては.
examples[].german: Depending on how you look at it, even this failure is a good experience.
Depending on how you go about it, you can finish it faster.
Depending on how you see it, his remark could also be taken as rude.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ようがなく ("with no way to") contradicts the positive reinterpretation in the main clause.
ようにも requires the volitional form and a negation (考えようにも考えられない).
ようとして ("while trying to") does not fit an evaluation like いい経験だ.

en.explanation: ようとしない expresses that someone does not even make an attempt to do something. Critical undertone.
en.formation: Verb-よう形 + としない
en.notes: Implies criticism of the lack of will.
examples[].german: The child won't eat vegetables (won't even try).
He won't even admit his mistake.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attempted action is linked with と.
The negative is not formed with ますない.
This asserts an attempt instead of its absence.

en.explanation: ずじまい describes how you intended to do something, or should have, but never did it right up to the end, and the opportunity is now gone. It sounds regretful or disappointed. Usually as ずじまいだった or ずじまいで; する becomes せずじまい.
en.formation: Verb (ない-stem) + ずじまい (する → せずじまい)
en.notes: ～ないまま is neutral ("without"), whereas ずじまい emphasizes that the chance is gone for good and sounds regretful. Don't confuse it with ～ずにすむ (N4, "don't have to, be spared"), which expresses relief. じまい comes from しまう ("to finish").
examples[].german: I was so busy during the trip that I never got to see him in the end.
I have lots of clothes that I went to the trouble of buying but never wore even once.
Who the forgotten items belonged to was never found out.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ずにはいられない ("can't help but") contradicts the meaning, and だった cannot attach directly to いられない.
ずにすむ expresses relief ("didn't have to") and does not come before だった.
ざるを得ない ("have no choice but to") fits neither the meaning nor the position before だった.

en.meaning: can't help but, can't help doing
en.explanation: ずにはいられない expresses that you cannot suppress a feeling or impulse. You do it involuntarily.
en.formation: Verb ない-stem + ずにはいられない (する → せずにはいられない)
en.notes: More emotional than ざるを得ない. Refers to feelings/impulses.
examples[].german: Whenever I watch this movie, I can't help crying.
Whenever I hear his jokes, I can't help laughing.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This affirms that it is possible to hold back the tears.
ない does not take an attached ます.
The set combination needs に.

en.explanation: ずくめ is attached to nouns and forms a な-adjective expressing that something consists exclusively or entirely of a particular thing. Unlike ～だらけ (chaotic/negative), ずくめ can be either positive or neutral.
en.formation: Noun + ずくめ (+ の/だ)
en.notes: Common combinations: 黒ずくめ (all in black), いいことずくめ (nothing but good things), ルールずくめ (full of rules), 異例ずくめ (one exception after another).
examples[].german: Today was a day full of nothing but good things.
A man dressed all in black was standing there.
Nothing but good things happened today.
He's dressed entirely in black.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not fit before the following modifier の一日.
な and の cannot attach together here.
ます cannot be attached directly to ずくめ.

en.explanation: 謝る (あやまる): to apologize. Japanese has various ways of apologizing depending on the situation and level of politeness.
en.formation: 謝る / ～てすみません / ～て申し訳ありません / ～てごめんなさい
en.notes: Politeness: ごめん(なさい) < すみません < 申し訳ありません/ございません. 謝る is the verb 'to apologize'.
examples[].german: I apologized for being late.
I'm sorry for the inconvenience.
Sorry I'm late.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: An apology for a circumstance needs the て-connection.
The ます-form does not form a connection here.
This is not a form of apology.

en.explanation: ～ば～ほど links two changes: "The more A, the more B." The same word appears twice – first in the ば-form, then in the dictionary form before ほど. The second part of the sentence describes what changes to the same degree.
en.formation: Verb (ば-form) + verb (dictionary form) + ほど / い-adj: ～ければ + ～い + ほど / な-adj: ～なら + ～な + ほど
en.notes: The ば part can be left out: 練習するほど上手になる. With な-adjectives: ～なら～なほど (formal: ～であればあるほど). Typical mistakes: putting the second verb in the た-form, or using たら instead of ば. ～ほど on its own (N4) can also express an extent: 泣きたいほど (so much that …).
examples[].german: The more you practice, the better you get.
The closer to the station, the higher the rent.
The simpler an explanation is, the better.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The construction requires the ば-form, not たら.
The dictionary form comes before ほど, not the た-form.
まで ("until") doesn't give "the more …, the more".

en.explanation: ばいいのに: expresses an unfulfilled wish or regret.
en.formation: Verb (ば-form) + いいのに
en.notes: Your own wish, or a reproach to someone else.
examples[].german: If only you'd said so sooner.
I wish it were sunny every day.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adjective いい does not take ます.
The fixed wish expression is のに.
The past of いい is よかった.

en.explanation: ばかりか: not only X, but Y as well.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + ばかりか ～も/さえ
en.notes: More formal than ～だけでなく.
examples[].german: He can speak not only Japanese but also Chinese.
Not only did my grades go up, I also made more friends.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: しか requires a negative ending.
を does not form a 'not only ... but also' connection here.
な does not connect to the following clause here.

en.explanation: ばかりに: just because of one particular reason, things turned out badly.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + ばかりに
en.notes: Always a negative result. Expresses regret.
examples[].german: Just because I was late, I missed the important talk.
Just because I had no money, I gave up on my dream.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The causal connection requires に.
No な is inserted after the verb.
の needs a following noun instead of the next clause.

en.meaning: manner, way of; for the first time in (a period)
en.explanation: ぶり has two meanings: 1) the way something is done, 2) again after a long time.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + ぶり / Time period + ぶり
en.notes: 久しぶり = it's been a long time. ～ぶりに = for the first time in.
examples[].german: I went to Japan for the first time in three years.
His way of working is wonderful.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means three years ago instead of again after three years.
This means after three years without expressing that it happened again.
This distributes amounts per three years instead of naming the gap before it happened again.

en.explanation: だらけ: covered with or full of something, usually with a negative connotation.
en.formation: Noun + だらけ
en.notes: Negative: 泥だらけ (covered in mud), 傷だらけ (covered in scratches).
examples[].german: The room is full of trash.
This essay is full of mistakes.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No additional な goes before だ.
に does not form a predicate ending here.
を does not connect to the copula here.

en.explanation: どころではない: the situation doesn't allow you to deal with that.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + どころではない / Noun + どころではない
en.notes: Informal: ～どころじゃない.
examples[].german: I'm so busy that a trip is out of the question.
This is no time for playing around!
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This affirms that there is room for a trip.
The set phrase uses では.
No だ follows ない.

en.explanation: どころか: reality is far from what was expected.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + どころか
en.notes: Intensifies the contrast between expectation and reality.
examples[].german: Forget a trip, I can't even take a day off.
Far from decreasing, it's increasing.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This is not an escalating contrast.
This is not an escalating contrast.
This does not connect the following clause.

en.explanation: 気味 (ぎみ): a slight condition or tendency, usually negative.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + 気味 / Noun + 気味
en.notes: Usually a slightly negative tendency. Behaves like a な-adjective: ～気味の + noun.
examples[].german: I've been putting on a bit of weight lately.
I have a slight cold and feel sluggish.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No additional な goes before だ.
An adverbial ending does not fit directly before だ.
を does not connect to the copula here.

en.explanation: 反面: shows the flip side or the opposite of a quality.
en.formation: Verb/Adj (plain form) + 反面
en.notes: Similar to ～一方で, but emphasizes the contrast more strongly.
examples[].german: This job is rewarding, but it's also very stressful.
The city is convenient, but the rent is high.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not form a contrastive connection here.
This does not connect the following clause.

en.explanation: ほかない: there is no other option.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + ほかない/よりほかない
en.notes: Similar: ～しかない, ～ざるを得ない.
examples[].german: There's nothing for it but to do it myself.
I had no choice but to walk home.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
This is not a construction meaning 'nothing but'.
No だ follows ない.

en.explanation: じゃん is a very casual contraction of じゃないか. You use it to seek agreement or to point out something obvious – often with surprise or a slight reproach. It originally comes from the area around Yokohama and is now widespread nationwide among younger people.
en.formation: Verb / い-adj (plain form) + じゃん; noun / な-adj + じゃん
en.notes: Only among friends; rude toward superiors. More polite equivalent: ～じゃないですか. Despite the form, it's not a negation: かわいいじゃん means "it's cute, isn't it", not "it isn't cute".
examples[].german: This outfit is so cute!
See, I told you!
We're off tomorrow, right? Let's go out and have some fun!
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: い-adjectives don't take だ: かわいいだ is ungrammatical.
かわいいでした is ungrammatical; the polite past would be かわいかったです.
じゃなかった is a real past negative and doesn't fit the compliment.

en.meaning: as long as, as far as
en.explanation: 限り: as long as a state lasts / as far as one knows.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/ない形/ている) + 限り
en.notes: できる限り = as much as possible.
examples[].german: As far as I know, there's no problem.
As long as I'm healthy, I want to keep working.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not fit before では here.
だ does not fit before では here.

en.explanation: からこそ: puts strong emphasis on the reason. 'Precisely BECAUSE...'.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + だからこそ
en.notes: Emphasizes the reason as especially important and positive.
examples[].german: It's precisely because I care about you that I'm strict.
There are things I was able to learn precisely because I failed.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The emphatic causal form contains no を.
の needs a noun, not 厳しくする.
だ does not connect a following clause here.

en.explanation: からには: once you've committed to something, you have to see it through.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/た形) + からには
en.notes: Similar: ～以上は.
examples[].german: If I'm going to do it, I'll see it through to the end.
Since I promised, I have to keep my word.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
The fixed premise construction contains no の.
This is not a premise construction.

en.explanation: からといって: just because X, it doesn't automatically mean Y.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + からといって ～わけではない
en.notes: Often with ～わけではない or ～とは限らない.
examples[].german: Just because it's cheap doesn't mean the quality is bad.
Just because you're Japanese doesn't mean you can read every kanji.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: In the standard language, 言う becomes 言って.
An い-adjective does not take な here.
The quoting connection requires と.

en.explanation: かわりに: 1) instead of doing something, 2) in return.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + かわりに / Noun + のかわりに
en.notes: An exchange/something in return, or an alternative.
examples[].german: Instead of buying a car, I went with a bicycle.
In return for my helping you, treat me to a meal.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not form an 'instead of' connection here.
の needs a following noun.

en.explanation: 謙譲語 (けんじょうご): lowers your own actions to elevate the person you are talking to.
en.formation: お + Verb (ます-stem) + する / 特別な形 (参る, 申す etc.)
en.notes: Special forms: 行く/来る→参る, 言う→申す, する→いたす, 見る→拝見する.
examples[].german: I will show you the way (humble).
May I visit you tomorrow (humble)?
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This negates showing the way.
The polite form is いたします.
Here the humble action is connected with いたす.

en.explanation: 尊敬語 (そんけいご): elevates other people's actions to show respect.
en.formation: お + Verb (ます-stem) + になる / 特別な形 (いらっしゃる, おっしゃる etc.)
en.notes: Special forms: いる→いらっしゃる, 言う→おっしゃる, 食べる→召し上がる, する→なさる.
examples[].german: The teacher has already gone home (respectful).
The company president said so (respectful).
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: お～になる requires the verb stem.
This negates going home.
The honorific expression uses に.

en.explanation: 決して strengthens a negative into "never, by no means". It sounds serious and emphatic and often appears in promises, warnings and assurances. In everyday speech it sounds rather written or solemn; casually you say 絶対(に)～ない.
en.formation: 決して + verb (ない / ません) / adj (～くない / ～ではない) / ～てはいけない
en.notes: 決して is only used with a negative or a prohibition – *決して行きます is wrong. 絶対(に), on the other hand, works both ways (絶対行く / 絶対行かない). Scale of intensifiers: 全然～ない (not at all, casual), 少しも / ちっとも～ない (not a bit), 決して～ない (never, serious).
examples[].german: I will never tell anyone about this.
This river is dangerous, so never swim in it!
Japanese is by no means easy, but it's a lot of fun.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 必ず ("certainly") is used with positive statements, not before a negative.
ぜひ is used with wishes and requests and doesn't fit a promise to keep quiet.
まるで ("as if") requires a comparison with ～ようだ.

en.explanation: ～気がする expresses a vague, intuitive impression: "I have a feeling that …" or "Somehow it seems to me that …". It is less certain and more personal than ～と思う and is useful for voicing an opinion cautiously. With nouns: ～ような気がする.
en.formation: Verb / い-adj (plain form) + 気がする / な-adj + な + 気がする / noun + の + ような気がする
en.notes: Describes your own impression; about others: ～気がするらしい. Don't confuse it with 気にする (to worry about), 気になる (to be on one's mind) and ～気がない (to not feel like it). Compared with ～と思う, 気がする is more intuitive and less reasoned.
examples[].german: I feel like I've met this person somewhere before.
Lately I feel like time goes by so fast.
Today I feel like I could do anything.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 気にする means "to worry about" and cannot take a clause as its content.
気がある means "to be interested" and doesn't fit a guess.
Feelings take が with する, not を.

en.explanation: きり: nothing has changed since a certain point, or only this one thing.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + きり / Noun + きり
en.notes: ～たきり = since (negative). ～きり = only (二人きり = just the two of us).
examples[].german: I met him once, and I haven't heard from him since.
I want to talk, just the two of us (alone).
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ながら does not follow the た-form.
会ったてから is not a valid verb connection.
No な is inserted after the verb.

en.explanation: っけ: you are trying to remember something or checking again.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun (た形/だ) + っけ
en.notes: Informal. Expresses that you have forgotten something and want to recall it.
examples[].german: What day is it tomorrow again?
What was that person's name again?
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a recollecting question here.
へ does not form a recollecting question here.
だます is not a sentence-final form.

en.explanation: っこない: colloquial, expresses absolute impossibility.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + っこない
en.notes: Very colloquial. Stronger than ～はずがない.
examples[].german: An exam that hard? There's no way I'll pass.
There's no way I can beat that person.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The fixed emphatic negative is っこない.
No だ follows ない.
っこない follows the stem 受かり.

en.explanation: ことだ: gives advice or a general recommendation.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/ない形) + ことだ
en.notes: General advice, not aimed at a specific person.
examples[].german: For your health, you should eat vegetables.
You shouldn't be late.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not go before this copula.
This is not a sentence ending.

en.explanation: ことから: gives the reason for, or origin of, a name or conclusion.
en.formation: Verb/Adj (plain form) + ことから
en.notes: Often used to explain names or origins.
examples[].german: Because its shape resembles a star, it's called a star fruit.
He was arrested on the grounds that he was the culprit.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
This is not a causal connection.
の does not connect a following predicate here.

en.explanation: ことなく: formal variant of ～ないで/～ずに.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + ことなく
en.notes: More formal than ～ないで/～ずに.
examples[].german: I kept making an effort without giving up.
I worked without taking a single break.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial phrase does not use を.
No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not attach an accompanying circumstance here.

en.meaning: to be planned/scheduled; to be the rule (extended)
en.explanation: ことになっている at N3: extended use for plans and social norms.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + ことになっている
en.notes: A social norm or a fixed plan.
examples[].german: A new project is scheduled to start next month.
In Japan, it's customary to take off your shoes.
At this school, you're supposed to wear a uniform.
Smoking is not allowed here.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The construction for something decided uses に.
No な is inserted after the verb.
This denies the existing plan.

en.meaning: to make it a rule to
en.explanation: ことにしている: a personal rule or habit that you keep deliberately.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/ない形) + ことにしている
en.notes: Emphasizes a conscious personal decision that has become a habit.
examples[].german: I make it a rule to go jogging every morning.
I make a point of not looking at my phone after 9 p.m.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The personal rule uses に.
No な is inserted after the verb.
This negates the personal rule.

en.explanation: くらい/ぐらい: indicates an extent or expresses 'about'.
en.formation: Verb/adj. + くらい / Number + くらい
en.notes: As extent: ～くらい = so much that. As an estimate: ～くらい = about.
examples[].german: I'm so frustrated I could cry.
I waited about thirty minutes.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ながら does not attach to たい.
This makes the wish to cry the reason instead of the degree of frustration.
泣きたいすぎて is not a correct connection.

en.explanation: くせに: like ～のに, but with a negative, reproachful nuance.
en.formation: Verb/adj. + くせに / Noun + のくせに
en.notes: Stronger and more negative than ～のに. Expresses annoyance.
examples[].german: He knows, yet he won't tell me.
He's just a kid, but he's so cheeky.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not connect contrasting statements here.
の cannot connect the following clause here.

en.explanation: ～ますように expresses a wish or prayer whose fulfillment is out of your hands: "May …". Typical at shrines, on Tanabata wish slips and in greetings. The ます-form is kept even when you're talking to yourself.
en.formation: Verb (ます-form) + ように / negative: ～ませんように
en.notes: Not for things you control yourself: *毎日勉強しますように – use ～ようにする or ～つもりだ for that. Common on cards: 早く良くなりますように (Get well soon). Related: ～ように (purpose, N4) and ～ように言う (telling someone to do something, N3).
examples[].german: Please let me pass the exam!
I hope it doesn't rain tomorrow!
May the new year be a good one for all of you.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ませんように wishes for the opposite: not passing the exam.
たい cannot combine with ように to form a wish.
ようだ (apparently) follows the plain form, not ます.

en.explanation: ものだ has three meanings: 1) general truth/what one should do, 2) reminiscence, 3) amazement.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/た形) + ものだ
en.notes: 辞書形 = should/general truth. た形 = reminiscence. よく～たものだ = recalling something you often did.
examples[].german: You should respect your elders.
When I was a child, I often used to play here.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not go before this copula.
The attributive form does not end the sentence.

en.explanation: ものの: concedes something but then expresses a contradiction. Formal.
en.formation: Verb/Adj (plain form) + ものの
en.notes: More formal than ～けど/～のに.
examples[].german: I bought it, but I haven't used it even once.
Although I'm studying Japanese, I still can't speak it well.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This makes the purchase the cause instead of a contrast.
No な is inserted after the verb.
This is not a concessive connection.

en.explanation: 向け: indicates the target group something is intended for.
en.formation: Noun + 向け(の) + Noun
en.notes: 向け = target group. 向き = suitable for (n3-muki).
examples[].german: There are a lot of programs for children.
This is Japanese learning material for foreigners.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 向けるの is not an attributive target-group marker here.
No additional adverbial ending に fits before の番組.
子供を向けた would mean pointing the children somewhere, not aiming programs at them.

en.explanation: 向き: expresses that something is suitable for a certain group.
en.formation: Noun + 向き(の) + Noun
en.notes: 向き = suitable. 向け = aimed at.
examples[].german: This book is suitable for beginners.
I'm looking for a family-friendly restaurant.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: An adverbial ending does not fit directly before だ.
This is not a noun-like expression of suitability here.
初心者を向くだ is not a fitting sentence ending.

en.explanation: ないことには: without this precondition, the outcome is not possible.
en.formation: Verb (ない形) + ことには
en.notes: Emphasizes that a precondition is necessary.
examples[].german: You won't know until you try.
I can't confirm it without asking the person themselves.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The necessary precondition uses には.
This is not a connection for the precondition.
だ does not belong after the precondition expression.

en.explanation: ないことはない: a double negative = a weak affirmative. 'It's possible, but...'
en.formation: Verb (ない形) + ことはない
en.notes: A weak affirmative with reservations.
examples[].german: It's not that I can't eat it, but I don't like it.
It's not that I don't understand it, but it's hard to explain.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This concedes inability instead of basic ability.
The qualifying double negative uses は.
No だ follows ない.

en.explanation: なんて and なんか highlight a word and give it an emotional coloring: contempt (宿題なんか), modesty (私なんか) or surprise (～なんて！). なんか is the casual form of など; only なんて can take up and comment on a whole sentence.
en.formation: Noun + なんか / なんて; sentence (plain form) + なんて; なんて + noun = "such a …"
en.notes: Three uses: (1) dismissive: 野菜なんか嫌い, (2) humble: 私なんかまだまだです, (3) surprised or indignant about a situation: ～なんて！ Used neutrally, なんか can also give examples (≈ など): お茶なんかどう？ Said about other people, the dismissive coloring can easily come across as rude.
examples[].german: Someone like me could never do such a difficult job.
Him quitting the company – I can't believe it!
I really don't feel like doing homework anymore!
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: こそ cannot come before には and would emphasize "precisely me".
The order would be 私にさえ; 私さえには is ungrammatical.
しか has to come after the particle (私にしか) and means "only me".

en.explanation: に違いない: strong conviction that something is the case.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + に違いない
en.notes: Stronger than ～はずだ. Almost 100% certainty.
examples[].german: He must know.
That sound must be a cat.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The fixed expression of certainty requires に.
The negative form is 違いない.
No な is inserted after the verb.

en.explanation: ～に限る expresses the personal conviction that something is the best choice: "When it comes to …, nothing beats …". It is often preceded by a situation (暑い日は…). It is a subjective recommendation from experience, not an objective fact.
en.formation: Noun + に限る / verb (dictionary form / ない-form) + に限る
en.notes: Similar-looking forms have other meanings: ～に限って (of all times, N2), ～に限らず (not only, N2), ～に限り (only for: 先着百名に限り). ～に限る is always a personal recommendation at the end of a sentence. More matter-of-fact: ～のが一番だ.
examples[].german: On hot days, nothing beats a cold beer.
When you have a cold, the best thing is to go to bed early.
It's best to stay out of troublesome matters.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: に限って ("of all times") cannot come at the end of a sentence.
に限らず ("not only") requires a following clause.
にすぎない ("merely, just") belittles the beer instead of recommending it.

en.explanation: にかかわらず: the outcome doesn't change, whatever the condition.
en.formation: Noun + にかかわらず / Verb (辞書形/ない形) + にかかわらず
en.notes: More formal than ～に関係なく. Don't confuse it with ～にもかかわらず (despite).
examples[].german: The match will be held regardless of the weather.
Please attend, whether you agree or not.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The negative form is かかわらず.
The set phrase uses に.
の does not attach to a verb here.

en.explanation: にかけて: from one point to another, usually with ～から.
en.formation: Noun + から + Noun + にかけて
en.notes: Often with ～から: AからBにかけて = from A to B.
examples[].german: It will probably rain from the afternoon into the evening.
There was an earthquake from Kantō to Tōhoku.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means only afterwards instead of through to the evening.
The て-form of かける is かけて.
をかけて does not express a time span starting from 午後から here.

en.explanation: に関して: the formal variant of ～について. Common in writing and reports.
en.formation: Noun + に関して / に関する + Noun
en.notes: More formal than ～について. Before nouns: ～に関する.
examples[].german: I have a question regarding this matter.
Environmental problems are increasing.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This marks a comparison rather than the topic of the question.
This marks a standard of value rather than the topic of the question.
This does not mark the topic of a question here.

en.explanation: にかわって: someone takes over another person's role or position.
en.formation: Noun + にかわって/にかわり
en.notes: Also: ～のかわりに (more informal).
examples[].german: The vice president gave the greeting on behalf of the president.
Email has spread and replaced letters.
The vice president gave the greeting on behalf of the president.
Email has replaced letters as the main means of communication.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This adds the vice president instead of standing in for the president.
The expression for standing in uses に.
The て-form of かわる is かわって.

en.explanation: に決まっている: the speaker is absolutely certain.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + に決まっている
en.notes: Very subjective and colloquial. Stronger than ～に違いない.
examples[].german: If you do something like that, you're bound to get told off.
That restaurant is bound to be good.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The fixed expression of certainty requires に.
The て-form of 決まる is 決まって.
No な is inserted after the verb.

en.explanation: に比べて: expresses a comparison between two things.
en.formation: Noun + に比べて
en.notes: Similar to ～より, but more formal and explicit.
examples[].german: Compared to last year, sales have grown.
Compared to Tokyo, prices in Osaka are lower.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This marks a contradiction rather than the comparison over time.
This names a topic rather than the standard of comparison.
A year is a standard of comparison here, not a standard of value.

en.explanation: にもかかわらず: formal variant of ～のに (despite).
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + にもかかわらず
en.notes: Very formal/written. Everyday language: ～のに.
examples[].german: Despite the rain, many people gathered.
Despite my efforts, I failed.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The negative form is かかわらず.
The set phrase requires に.
の does not connect a following clause here.

en.meaning: based on, on the basis of
en.explanation: に基づいて: something is done on the basis of facts or rules.
en.formation: Noun + に基づいて / に基づく + Noun
en.notes: Before nouns: ～に基づく/～に基づいた.
examples[].german: Making a judgment on the basis of the law.
It's a film based on true events.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means against the law.
This means regardless of the law.
This makes the law the subject matter rather than the basis for the judgment.

en.explanation: において: the formal variant of ～で (place/domain). Written language.
en.formation: Noun + において / における + Noun
en.notes: Before nouns: ～における. Very formal/written.
examples[].german: The conference was held in Tokyo.
Thinking about problems in modern society.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This makes Tokyo the topic of the conference rather than its venue.
This does not name a venue.
This means instead of Tokyo, not in Tokyo.

en.explanation: に応じて: adapting to circumstances or conditions.
en.formation: Noun + に応じて / に応じた + Noun
en.notes: Similar: ～に合わせて, ～次第で.
examples[].german: Changing your response depending on the situation.
Giving work that matches someone's abilities.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means contrary to the situation rather than in line with it.
This means regardless of the situation rather than depending on it.
状況に関する対応 means a response concerning the situation, not the required dependence of how the response changes.

en.meaning: in accordance with, following; as ... (proportional change)
en.explanation: に従って: following a rule/instruction, or a proportional change.
en.formation: Noun + に従って / Verb (辞書形) + に従って
en.notes: Rule: ～に従って + action. Proportional: like ～につれて.
examples[].german: Please work according to the instructions.
As the altitude rises, the temperature drops.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This would mean acting against the instructions.
This would mean ignoring the instructions.
The て-form of 従う is 従って.

en.explanation: にしては: the result differs from what you would expect of X.
en.formation: Noun/verb + にしては
en.notes: Implies: 'considering that...'.
examples[].german: You're good for a beginner.
He's tall for a Japanese person.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: の needs a following noun instead of 上手ですね.
This makes beginners the source of information instead of the standard of comparison.
This means regardless of being a beginner, not surprisingly good for one.

en.meaning: along; in line with, in accordance with
en.explanation: に沿って: following a line, a plan or a guideline.
en.formation: Noun + に沿って / に沿った + Noun
en.notes: Works both concretely (a river) and abstractly (a plan).
examples[].german: I walked along the river.
Please proceed according to the plan.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means away from the river instead of along it.
The standard て-form is 沿って.
沿う is connected with に here.

en.explanation: に伴って: a change that takes place alongside another one.
en.formation: Noun + に伴って / に伴い / に伴う + Noun
en.notes: Formal. Similar: ～につれて, ～とともに.
examples[].german: Along with population growth, environmental problems became more serious.
Changes that come with economic growth can be seen.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means against the population growth.
This claims independence rather than an accompanying change.
This names a standard of value rather than a parallel development.

en.explanation: にとっての: attributive form of にとって, used before nouns.
en.formation: Noun + にとっての + Noun
en.notes: にとって + clause vs. にとっての + noun.
examples[].german: For me, happiness is spending time with my family.
The biggest challenge for students is finding a job.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The attributive perspective is connected with の.
を does not fit before 幸せ here.
を取っての is not the perspective construction here.

en.explanation: につれて: two changes happen in parallel.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + につれて / Noun + につれて
en.notes: Similar: ～に伴って (more formal), ～に従って (following a rule).
examples[].german: As you get older, your physical strength declines.
As time passes, you forget.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The fixed construction for change ends in て here.
を連れて means taking someone along and does not connect to 年を取る.
ながら requires the stem, not 年を取る.

en.explanation: にわたって: expresses that something covers a wide area or a long period.
en.formation: Noun + にわたって / にわたる + Noun
en.notes: Before nouns: ～にわたる. Emphasizes extent in time or space.
examples[].german: The conference was held over three days.
A survey covering a wide area was carried out.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means before the period.
This means after the period.
The て-form of わたる is わたって.

en.explanation: ～により is the written form of ～によって and appears in the news and in announcements, especially for causes: 大雪により (due to heavy snow). ～による comes before a noun: 台風による被害. The meanings are the same as for によって.
en.formation: Noun + により + clause / noun + による + noun
en.notes: Register: で (spoken: 事故で遅れた) – によって (neutral) – により (written, announcements). Before a noun it's always による: 専門家による説明. Don't confuse it with ～によると (according to a source). A typical platform announcement: 人身事故により、運転を見合わせております.
examples[].german: Trains are stopped due to heavy snow.
The damage caused by the typhoon was greater than expected.
The rules differ from country to country.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: による must come before a noun; before a clause you need により or によって.
によると names a source of information ("according to"), not a cause.
に対して means "toward, in contrast to" and gives no reason for the stoppage.

en.meaning: isn't it the case that …? (cautious guess)
en.explanation: ～のではないか expresses a cautious guess or opinion: "Couldn't it be that …?" Although the form looks negative, it affirms the statement. It is often followed by と思う or と心配する. In conversation: ～んじゃないか / ～んじゃない？
en.formation: Verb / い-adj (plain form) + のではないか / noun・な-adj + な + のではないか; spoken: ～んじゃないか
en.notes: Difference: ～のではないか (guess, affirmative) vs. ～のではない (real negation: "it's not that …"). ～のではないでしょうか is a popular, polite way to state your own opinion in discussions without sounding too direct. Colloquially with rising intonation: ～んじゃない？
examples[].german: Isn't this plan a bit unrealistic?
I think she's probably gone home already.
I'm worried that tomorrow's game might be canceled.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: Without か, the statement becomes a real negation ("it's not that") instead of a guess.
の is missing after 無理な; な cannot come directly before では.
The form requires では; のは does not express a guess.

en.meaning: to see through to the end, to do thoroughly
en.explanation: 抜く as a suffix: carrying a difficult action through to completion.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + 抜く
en.notes: 考え抜く (to think through thoroughly), 悩み抜く (to agonize at length).
examples[].german: I ran all the way to the end.
I overcame the difficulties and saw it through.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This negates the persevering.
This is not a past form.
ます does not go between the verbs.

en.meaning: with ... at the center, focusing on
en.explanation: を中心に: something is at the center or in focus.
en.formation: Noun + を中心に(して)
en.notes: Also: ～を中心として (more formal).
examples[].german: The town developed around the station.
I'm studying with a focus on grammar.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This moves the development far away from the station.
The adverbial connection requires に.
This is not an adverbial connection to 発展した.

en.explanation: をはじめ: highlights a main example and implies there are more.
en.formation: Noun + をはじめ(として)
en.notes: Formal. The item named with をはじめ is the most important example.
examples[].german: I visited countries in Asia, starting with Japan.
All the employees took part, starting with the company president.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This does not express a highlighted start of a list.
This means instead of Japan rather than including Japan.
This excludes Japan, even though it was explicitly visited.

en.explanation: をきっかけに: an event becomes the trigger for a change.
en.formation: Noun/verb (た形) + のをきっかけに
en.notes: The trigger is usually a single, concrete event.
examples[].german: Studying abroad was what got me to start learning Japanese.
My illness prompted me to rethink my lifestyle.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial trigger expression requires に.
This is not an adverbial connection.
The attributive form would be をきっかけにした, not をきっかけの.

en.explanation: を込めて: something is done with a particular feeling or effort put into it.
en.formation: Noun + を込めて
en.notes: 心を込めて (wholeheartedly), 願いを込めて (with a wish).
examples[].german: I made it with all my heart.
I gave a present as a token of my gratitude.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The て-form of 込める is 込めて.
The feeling put into it is marked with を.
This means without putting your heart into it, which contradicts the translation.

en.explanation: を問わず: it doesn't matter which case applies.
en.formation: Noun + を問わず
en.notes: Formal. Common: 国籍を問わず, 男女を問わず.
examples[].german: Anyone can take part, regardless of age.
Anyone can apply, with or without experience.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The negative form of 問う is 問わず.
The set phrase uses を.
だ does not connect a following clause here.

en.explanation: を通じて/を通して: via a medium or throughout a period of time.
en.formation: Noun + を通じて/を通して
en.notes: を通じて = more abstract/a medium. を通して = also concrete/a period of time.
examples[].german: Connecting with the world through the internet.
The climate is warm all year round.
Through the internet, you can interact with people all over the world.
The climate is mild all year round.
I learned a lot through volunteer work.
I want to live in an area that is warm all year round.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means avoiding the internet.
This means regardless of the internet.
This means against the internet rather than by means of it.

en.explanation: おきに: expresses regular intervals.
en.formation: Number + time unit + おきに
en.notes: 一日おきに = every other day. 一つおきに = every other one.
examples[].german: Please take the medicine every two hours.
I go jogging every other day.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The interval expression requires に.
を does not form an interval expression here.
This means two hours ago instead of every two hours.

en.meaning: there is a risk that, there is a danger of
en.explanation: おそれがある: formally warns of a possible negative outcome.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + おそれがある / Noun + のおそれがある
en.notes: Formal. Often used in news reports and warnings.
examples[].german: There is a risk that a typhoon will approach.
There is a risk of an earthquake.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ある does not take a direct object here.
No な is inserted after the verb.
This denies the danger.

en.explanation: っぱなし: a state stays unchanged, often with a negative connotation.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + っぱなし
en.notes: Often critical: 出しっぱなし (left out), 立ちっぱなし (standing the whole time).
examples[].german: Don't leave the door open.
I fell asleep with the TV on.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No additional な fits before にしないで.
This is not the noun for the state left as it is here.
The construction requires っぱなしにする.

en.explanation: っぽい at N3 level: further nuances and uses.
en.formation: Noun/verb stem + っぽい
en.notes: 忘れっぽい (forgetful), 飽きっぽい (quickly bored).
examples[].german: This story sounds like a lie.
It's a grown-up-looking style of dress.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: An い-adjective does not take だ.
This is not an adjective form.
An adjective does not take ます.

en.explanation: さえ～ば: a single condition is enough.
en.formation: Noun + さえ + Verb (ば-form) / Verb (ます-stem) + さえすれば
en.notes: Emphasizes that only THIS ONE condition is needed.
examples[].german: As long as you have money, you can do anything.
All you have to do is take the medicine and you'll get better.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The conditional form of ある is あれば.
を does not go between さえ and あれば.
This reverses the necessary condition of having money.

en.explanation: 際に: formal variant of ～時に. Often used in official contexts.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/た形) + 際(に) / Noun + の際(に)
en.notes: Formal/written. Everyday language: ～時に.
examples[].german: When leaving, please take care not to forget anything.
ID is required when applying.
When leaving, please be careful not to leave anything behind.
ID is required when applying.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: No な is inserted before は here.
を does not fit before the topic-marked time expression with は.
The copula does not fit before は.

en.meaning: in the middle of, right while
en.explanation: 最中に: something happens right in the middle of an action.
en.formation: Verb (ている) + 最中に / Noun + の最中に
en.notes: Emphasizes that the action is in full swing.
examples[].german: The phone rang in the middle of the meeting.
A visitor came while I was in the middle of eating.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means before the meeting.
This means after the meeting.
The adverbial time expression requires に.

en.explanation: ～せいか gives a presumed reason, usually for something unpleasant: "perhaps because …". The speaker isn't sure whether the reason really applies. Unlike ～せいで, which clearly names a cause or puts the blame, ～せいか stays cautious.
en.formation: Verb / い-adj (plain form) + せいか / な-adj + な + せいか / noun + の + せいか
en.notes: Set phrase: 気のせい (one's imagination), 気のせいか = "maybe it's just my imagination". Occasionally also used for neutral or positive results (薬を飲んだせいか、よく眠れた), then without any sense of blame. Comparison: ～せいで (certain cause, negative), ～おかげで (certain cause, positive), ～せいか / ～ためか / ～からか (presumed cause).
examples[].german: Maybe it's from lack of sleep, but I have a headache today.
Maybe it's my age, but lately I get tired easily.
Maybe it's just my imagination, but she seems down today.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: せいに belongs to せいにする (to blame) and does not introduce a reason.
くせに means a reproachful "even though" and doesn't fit a reason.
ついでに means "while one is at it" and names no cause.

en.explanation: 次第: 1) as soon as something happens (ます-stem + 次第), 2) it depends on (noun + 次第).
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + 次第 / Noun + 次第
en.notes: ます-stem + 次第 = as soon as (formal). Noun + 次第 = it depends on.
examples[].german: I'll contact you as soon as it arrives.
The result depends on you.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 届きたら is not a verb form.
This does not connect the following action adverbially.
を does not form a time expression here.

en.explanation: たところ: when you tried something, a (often unexpected) result came about.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + ところ
en.notes: Difference from ～ところだ (point in time): ～たところ = result.
examples[].german: When I asked, it was already sold out.
When I looked into it, I found a problem.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: みるところ does not describe the result of asking here.
The expression does not follow the ます-form here.
な does not connect the following clause.

en.explanation: たところで: even if you do something, nothing changes / it's pointless.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + ところで
en.notes: Always a negative/resigned outcome.
examples[].german: Even if I apologize now, they won't forgive me.
Even if I hurry, I won't make it in time.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 謝っる is not a verb form.
を does not go before the concessive ending で.
謝っます is not a verb form.

en.explanation: たびに: every time an action takes place, something happens.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形) + たびに / Noun + のたびに
en.notes: Regular repetition.
examples[].german: Every time I go to Japan, I buy souvenirs.
Every time I hear this song, I remember my student days.
Every time I go to Japan, I discover something new.
Every time I hear this song, I'm reminded of my student days.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The repeated time expression requires に.
No な is inserted after the verb.
を does not form a repeated time expression here.

en.meaning: you should …; what should I do?
en.explanation: ～たらいい and ～ばいい give advice: "It's best to …" or "All you have to do is …". In questions like どうしたらいいですか / どうすればいいですか, you ask for advice. ばいい often stresses that a simple solution is enough; たらいい sounds a bit more conversational.
en.formation: Verb (たら-form) + いい / verb (ば-form) + いい; question: question word + ～たら / ～ば + いいですか
en.notes: Giving advice: ～たらいい / ～ばいい (neutral), ～といい (friendly recommendation), ～たほうがいい (clear advice, often with a warning). ～ばいい can also sound dismissive: 嫌ならやめればいい (If you don't like it, just quit). With のに it turns into regret or reproach: ～ばいいのに (N3).
examples[].german: What's the best way to get to the station?
If there's something you don't understand, just ask the teacher.
I've lost my wallet. What on earth should I do?
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ばいいのに expresses regret or reproach and cannot be used with ですか.
The ば-form is missing between 行け and いい; たいい is not a form.
行けるいい is ungrammatical; advice needs ～ばいい.

en.explanation: Verb stem + たて describes something that has just been made or done and is therefore still fresh: 焼きたてのパン (freshly baked bread). It is only usual with certain typical verbs, especially for food, and sounds positive.
en.formation: Verb stem (ます-form without ます) + たて + の + noun / + たてだ
en.notes: Typical words: 焼きたて, 揚げたて, 炊きたて (rice), できたて, 取れたて (freshly harvested), 生まれたて, 入社したて. ～たばかり (N4) is the general "just did" and works with any verb; たて stresses the freshness of the result. Counterpart: ～かけ (half-done, started).
examples[].german: Freshly baked bread is really delicious.
When I had just joined the company, I was nervous every day.
It says "Wet paint," so don't touch it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ばかり needs the た-form (焼いたばかり), not the verb stem.
～ぶり describes a manner or a time interval, not freshness.
～がち means "tends to" and doesn't fit bread.

en.explanation: たとえ signals early in the sentence that a concession with ～ても will follow: "Even if …, (nothing changes)". It sounds determined or solemn and is often used for hypothetical or extreme cases. The actual grammar is carried by ～ても / ～でも.
en.formation: たとえ + verb (て-form) + も / い-adj (～くても) / な-adj・noun + でも (or だとしても)
en.notes: たとえ alone doesn't change the grammar – what matters is ～ても / ～でも / ～としても at the end of the clause. もし goes with ～たら / ～ば (if), while たとえ is the typical signal word for ～ても (even if). Colloquial: たとえ～たって. Elevated: たとえ～であろうと.
examples[].german: Even if people oppose me, I will keep doing this job.
Even if it rains, the game will be held.
Even if it's just a joke, you shouldn't say something like that.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: たぶん ("probably") doesn't fit a concession with ても.
ぜひ is used with wishes and requests, not with "even if".
まるで ("as if") requires ～ようだ or ～みたい.

en.explanation: ～たって is the colloquial form of ～ても: "even if". It is formed from the た-form (走ったって, 高くたって); after nouns and な-adjectives it becomes ～だって. Typical of lively conversation, often with frustration or defiance.
en.formation: Verb (た-form) + って / い-adj: ～くたって / な-adj・noun + だって
en.notes: Equivalent to ～ても (N4), but sounds much more casual – avoid it in essays and polite speech. Often with いくら / どんなに (no matter how much) or 何度 (no matter how often). Noun + だって can also mean "too, even" (私だって行きたい = I want to go too!), and だって at the start of a sentence means a defiant "but, because".
examples[].german: Even if you run now, you won't make it.
No matter how expensive it is, I buy what I want.
However quiet it may be, I don't want an apartment far from the station.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: だって follows nouns and な-adjectives; the verb needs the た-form + って.
たって already contains the meaning of ても; たっても doubles it and is wrong.
でも cannot attach to the た-form.

en.explanation: て以来: since a certain event, with the state continuing.
en.formation: Verb (て-form) + 以来
en.notes: More formal than ～てから. The state after the event continues.
examples[].german: Since coming to Japan, I've been using Japanese every day.
I haven't seen him since graduating.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The time expression requires 来て以来.
以来 does not attach to ます here.
This means before rather than since arriving.

en.meaning: now is not the time to …
en.explanation: Literally "it is not a situation in which one does …". You state that an action is inappropriate under the circumstances because something more urgent needs attention.
en.formation: Verb (て-form) + いる + 場合じゃない / 場合ではない
en.notes: More formal: ～ている場合ではない. Related to ～どころではない (N3), which stresses that something is not possible at all under the circumstances. In conversation often shortened: 寝てる場合じゃない.
examples[].german: This is no time to be sleeping – it's time to go!
The test is tomorrow, so this is no time to be playing games.
This is no laughing matter – I'm really in trouble.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 寝てもいい permits sleeping and contradicts the following sentence.
寝たほうがいい advises sleeping – the opposite of the intended statement.
寝ているところだ only describes that you're sleeping right now and doesn't express that it's inappropriate.

en.explanation: てからでないと: an action has to be completed first.
en.formation: Verb (て-form) + からでないと/からでなければ
en.notes: Condition: first X, then Y becomes possible.
examples[].german: I can't answer until I've looked into it.
I can't tell until I've tried it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This is not a connection for checking first.
This is not a necessary precondition.
The time construction requires the て-form.

en.explanation: てこそ: only through this action does something become truly possible/worthwhile.
en.formation: Verb (て-form) + こそ
en.notes: Emphasizes that the action is an indispensable precondition.
examples[].german: Only by practicing do you get good.
It only has meaning if you do it yourself.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The necessary experience is connected with the て-form.
ます is not a connection for 'only by' here.
するて is not a て-form.

en.explanation: てならない: an involuntary feeling that you cannot control.
en.formation: Verb (て) + ならない / い-adj. (くて) + ならない
en.notes: More formal than ～てたまらない. Used mainly for emotional feelings.
examples[].german: I can't help worrying about him.
It's deeply regrettable.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 心配 is nominal/adjectival and connects with で here.
The negative form is ならない.
No だ follows the negative form.

en.explanation: てしかたがない/てしょうがない: a feeling is so strong that you can't do anything about it.
en.formation: Verb (て) + しかたがない / い-adj. (くて) + しかたがない
en.notes: しょうがない = more informal. Similar: ～てたまらない, ～てならない.
examples[].german: I'm so sleepy I can't help it.
It's so much fun I can't stop.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ない requires が here, not を.
眠く requires the て-connection.
This is not the set phrase for irresistible sleepiness.

en.explanation: てたまらない: a feeling or state is so strong that you can hardly bear it.
en.formation: Verb (て) + たまらない / い-adj. (くて) + たまらない
en.notes: Similar: ～てしかたがない, ～てならない. All = an unbearable feeling.
examples[].german: It's unbearably hot.
I want to see you so badly I can hardly stand it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: After 暑く, the て-connection is required.
The negative form is たまらない.
No だ follows the negative form.

en.explanation: 的 (てき): turns nouns into な-adjectives, much like the English suffixes '-ic' or '-al'.
en.formation: Noun + 的(な/に)
en.notes: Very productive: 国際的 (international), 一般的 (general), 基本的 (basic).
examples[].german: That's a Japanese way of thinking.
Please explain it concretely.
I take part actively.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: に must not be added before な考え方.
The attributive connection uses な.
だ does not go before な考え方 here.

en.explanation: ては～ては: two actions keep repeating in alternation.
en.formation: Verb (て) + は + Verb (て) + は
en.notes: Expresses tiresome repetition.
examples[].german: It's a life of eating and sleeping, eating and sleeping.
Writing and erasing, writing and erasing, over and over.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The repeated sequence needs the て-form.
ます does not link the repeated actions here.
食べるて is not a て-form.

en.meaning: speaking of …; when you think of …
en.explanation: ～といえば and ～というと take up a topic and name the first thing that comes to mind: "When you think of …, then …". In conversation, といえば also introduces a change of topic ("Speaking of …"). というと can additionally ask for clarification: "You mean …?"
en.formation: Noun + といえば / というと (/ といったら)
en.notes: といえば = spontaneous association, or "speaking of" when changing the topic. というと also works as a follow-up question: 「というと？」 = "Meaning?". The variant といったら often emphasizes a strong feeling. Don't confuse them with ～といっても (even though one says …, N2) or ～というのは (definition).
examples[].german: When you think of winter in Japan, it's hot springs, of course.
"I'm going to Kyōto next week." "Kyōto – that's the place with lots of temples, right?"
Speaking of travel, are you going anywhere over the summer vacation?
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: によって means "depending on" or "by"; here, though, a typical example is being named.
にしては expresses surprise at a deviation and contradicts やっぱり.
というのに means "even though" and needs a whole clause before it.

en.meaning: such as, like (examples before a noun)
en.explanation: AやBといったC gives examples of a group: "C such as A and B". The list isn't complete; it shows typical members. It sounds slightly more elevated than など and is often used in descriptions, the news and presentations.
en.formation: Noun (や / とか / 、) noun + といった + noun
en.notes: Difference from など: など can stand on its own (本などを買った), while といった always needs a noun after it that names the group. Don't confuse it with ～という (called: 田中という人) or the past tense 言った (said). Colloquial: AとかBみたいなC.
examples[].german: At this restaurant you can eat Japanese dishes such as sushi and tempura.
I like sports such as soccer and baseball.
We have staff who can speak languages such as English, Chinese and Korean.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: といって is a verb form and cannot modify a noun like 日本料理.
といっても means "even though one says" and needs a following clause, not a noun.
にとって means "for someone" and makes no sense here.

en.meaning: that's what ... is (the true nature of)
en.explanation: というものだ: emphasizes the true nature or essence of something.
en.formation: Noun/clause + というものだ
en.notes: Philosophical/instructive. というものではない = it's not that simple.
examples[].german: That is true friendship.
That's just how life is.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The defining expression uses と.
を does not go before this copula.
This is not a sentence ending here.

en.explanation: ～というのは takes up a word or statement as the topic in order to explain or define it: "X – that means …". It is often followed by ～のことだ or ～という意味だ. At the start of a sentence, というのは also introduces a reason: "The reason is that …".
en.formation: Noun / sentence (plain form) + というのは + explanation (～のことだ / ～という意味だ / ～からだ)
en.notes: For definitions it is similar to ～とは (written) and ～って (spoken). As a conjunction at the start of a sentence: というのは… ～からだ (you see, because). Don't confuse it with ～というと (association) or ～ということだ (that means / apparently).
examples[].german: "Tsundoku" means buying books and leaving them piled up unread.
"Shūkatsu" is short for job hunting.
I'll be absent tomorrow. The reason is that my mother has been admitted to the hospital.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: によって ("by, depending on") does not introduce a definition.
というのに means "even though" and gives no explanation here.
にとって ("for someone") doesn't fit an explanation of a term.

en.meaning: rather than …; not so much … as …
en.explanation: ～というより corrects or refines a description: "It's not so much A as B." You concede that A isn't entirely wrong but consider B more accurate. The second part often contains むしろ (rather).
en.formation: Noun / な-adj (without だ) / verb・い-adj (plain form) + というより (むしろ) + B
en.notes: Often strengthened: AというよりむしろB. Difference from ～より (AはBより高い): there, two things are compared; with というより, two descriptions of the same thing. Don't confuse it with ～どころか (far from it, rather the opposite). In conversation also at the start of a sentence: というより… = "Or rather …".
examples[].german: Today it's not so much warm as almost hot.
He's less a friend than something like family.
This book is less educational than simply fun to read.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: によって cannot come directly after an い-adjective.
にとって follows a noun and means "for someone".
としては follows a noun ("as …"), not an adjective.

en.explanation: としても: even if you assume that X is true.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + としても
en.notes: More hypothetical than ～ても.
examples[].german: Even if I fail, I won't regret it.
Even supposing I pass, there's still a long way to go.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The hypothetical assumption requires と.
The て-form of する is して.
No な is inserted after the verb.

en.meaning: assuming that …; if that's true, then …
en.explanation: ～とすると and ～とすれば set up an assumption and draw a conclusion from it: "If we assume that …, then …". The following clause is usually an assessment or guess, not an action.
en.formation: Verb / い-adj (plain form) + とすると・とすれば / noun・な-adj + だ + とすると・とすれば
en.notes: Almost the same as ～としたら (N2), which sounds a bit more hypothetical. ～としても, by contrast, means "even if" (concession). At the start of a sentence as a conjunction: とすると / とすれば = "so then …". For simple everyday conditions followed by an action, ～なら is more natural: 雨なら、傘を持っていこう.
examples[].german: If what he says is true, we're in serious trouble.
If you study three hours every day, that makes ninety hours in a month.
"I hear Mr. Yamada is off starting next week." "Then who's going to do this work?"
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: とは expresses surprise or a definition and does not introduce a conclusion.
ところで follows the た-form (～たところで) and means "even if …, it's no use".
にしては does not come after だ and means "considering (that)".

en.explanation: とは限らない: something does not apply in every case.
en.formation: Verb/adj./noun + とは限らない
en.notes: Rejects an overly simple generalization.
examples[].german: Expensive things aren't necessarily good.
Working hard doesn't necessarily mean you'll succeed.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This affirms the restriction instead of rejecting it.
The negative form is 限らない.
The quoted claim is connected with と.

en.explanation: とおりに: exactly as something was said/done/expected.
en.formation: Verb (た形/辞書形) + とおり(に) / Noun + のとおり(に)
en.notes: 言ったとおり (as I said), 予想どおり (as expected).
examples[].german: Please assemble it according to the instructions.
It was just as I thought.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial 'in line with' requires に.
を does not express manner here.
の needs a following noun instead of 組み立てて.

en.explanation: にしても～にしても: whichever the alternative, the outcome is the same.
en.formation: A + にしても + B + にしても
en.notes: Similar: ～ても～ても, ～にせよ～にせよ.
examples[].german: Whether you go or not, please let me know.
Whether you're for or against it, please give your reason.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: を does not form a hypothetical assumption here.
The て-form of する is して.
No な is inserted after the verb.

en.explanation: たとたん: right after an action, something unexpected happens.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + とたん(に)
en.notes: Always unexpected/surprising. Similar: ～た瞬間.
examples[].german: The moment I opened the door, the cat jumped out.
The moment I lay down, I fell asleep.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: After 開け this gives 開けるとたん; the sudden follow-up event requires the た-form.
な is not a clause connector here.
The expression does not follow the ます-form.

en.meaning: while one is at it; taking the opportunity
en.explanation: ～ついでに means using an opportunity to get something else done on the side: "while I'm at it, I'll also …". The first action is the real purpose, the second a convenient extra. Very common with errands and trips.
en.formation: Verb (dictionary form / た-form) + ついでに / noun + の + ついでに
en.notes: Both actions are intended, but the second is secondary. ～ながら, by contrast, links two simultaneous activities without a main and a secondary purpose. ～がてら (N1) is more literary and usually follows movement such as 散歩. As a noun: ついでがあったら… (if you get the chance).
examples[].german: Since you're going to the station anyway, could you mail this letter for me?
While I was out shopping, I also stopped by the post office.
While I was on a business trip to Osaka, I also went to see a friend in Kyōto.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ながら requires the verb stem (行きながら) and expresses simultaneity.
とたんに follows the た-form and means "the very moment".
次第 follows the verb stem (行き次第) and means "as soon as".

en.explanation: つつ: formal variant of ～ながら (at the same time) or ～のに (although).
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + つつ
en.notes: ～つつも = although. ～つつある = to be in the process of.
examples[].german: Even though I know it's bad, I end up eating it anyway.
I took a walk while enjoying the scenery.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 思いたら is not a verb form.
思いても is not the て-form of 思う.
思いないで is not a negative form.

en.meaning: to be in the process of, to be gradually changing
en.explanation: つつある: a gradual change is under way.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + つつある
en.notes: Formal/written. Similar: ～ている (process of change).
examples[].german: The situation is improving.
This culture is disappearing.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The fixed progressive form is つつある.
No だ follows ある.
つつ attaches to 改善し, not to 改善する.

en.explanation: ってば (from って言えば) gives impatient emphasis to a statement or request: you're repeating something the other person doesn't want to hear. After names it expresses affectionate annoyance.
en.formation: Sentence (plain form) / request + ってば; name + ってば
en.notes: Very colloquial and emotional; only used with people close to you. After people it is almost the same as ～ったら (N2). Don't confuse it with the conditional ～ば.
examples[].german: I'm fine, I told you! Don't worry.
Hurry up already!
Geez, Mom, you're saying the same thing again.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: ければ is the conditional of い-adjectives and cannot follow だ.
だっても is ungrammatical; the concessive would be でも.
ってた reports a past remark ("said") and adds no emphasis.

en.explanation: うちに: doing something while a state still lasts.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/ない形/ている) + うちに / Adj. + うちに
en.notes: ～ているうちに = while (and meanwhile something changes).
examples[].german: I want to experience lots of things while I'm young.
Let me make a note of it before I forget.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: An い-adjective does not take な here.
の would modify a noun instead of the following clause.
を does not form a time expression here.

en.explanation: 上で: 1) after doing something (た形), 2) in terms of, when it comes to ... (辞書形).
en.formation: Verb (た形/辞書形) + 上で / Noun + の上で
en.notes: た形 + 上で = after. 辞書形/noun + 上で = regarding.
examples[].german: Please decide after thinking it over carefully.
That's important when it comes to work.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The decision that follows requires 上で here.
前に requires the dictionary form and means beforehand.
ながら does not follow the た-form.

en.explanation: わけではない: partially negates an assumption: it's not quite like that.
en.formation: Verb/Adj (plain form) + わけではない
en.notes: Partial negation. ～わけがない = complete impossibility.
examples[].german: It's not that I dislike it, but I don't eat it much.
It's not that everyone agrees.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This affirms the dislike instead of rejecting the inference.
The negation is わけではない.
This concedes a dislike instead of denying it.

en.explanation: 割に: the result does not match what you would expect.
en.formation: Verb/adj. + 割に / Noun + の割に
en.notes: Expresses an unexpected result.
examples[].german: This restaurant is good for the price.
Considering I studied, my grades are bad.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The adverbial evaluation needs に.
This is not an adverbial evaluation of the price.
This does not express a price-quality comparison here.

en.explanation: ようがない: it is absolutely impossible to do something.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + ようがない
en.notes: どうしようもない = there is absolutely nothing you can do.
examples[].german: I don't know their contact details, so there's no way for me to get in touch.
It's a hopeless situation.
Since I don't know the address, there's no way to contact them.
Since there's no evidence, there's no way to prove it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The expression requires が.
This affirms that contact is possible.
ようがない follows the stem し.

en.meaning: to tell/ask someone to do something
en.explanation: ように言う: passing on an indirect request or instruction.
en.formation: Verb (辞書形/ない形) + ように言う/頼む/注意する
en.notes: Reported instructions. Also with 頼む, 注意する, etc.
examples[].german: The doctor told me to exercise.
I told the child to go to bed early.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The reported request requires に.
No な is inserted after the verb.
This negates the doctor's instruction.

en.meaning: cannot help but, have no choice but to
en.explanation: ざるを得ない: you have no choice but to do something.
en.formation: Verb (ない-stem) + ざるを得ない
en.notes: する→せざるを得ない. Formal. Similar: ～ないわけにはいかない.
examples[].german: I have no choice but to accept these conditions.
Due to circumstances, I had no choice but to quit.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The obligation construction needs the negative 得ない.
The set phrase requires を.
This advises against accepting.

en.explanation: づらい: something is psychologically or emotionally hard to do.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + づらい
en.notes: づらい = psychological difficulty. にくい = physical difficulty.
examples[].german: There are things that are hard to say to my boss.
These shoes are hard to walk in.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: An い-adjective modifies こと without な.
The adverbial form does not modify こと here.
The adjective modifies こと without の.

en.explanation: い-adjectives: い→ければ. な-adjectives: なら(ば).
en.formation: い-Adj: い→ければ / な-Adj: ～なら(ば)
en.notes: いい→よければ. Negative: ～くなければ / ～でなければ.
examples[].german: If it's cheap, I'll buy it.
If you're free, come over.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The い is dropped before ければ.
This is not a conditional form.
This reverses the condition: if it is not cheap.

en.explanation: そうな before nouns, そうに before verbs. A visual impression.
en.formation: い-Adj (without い) + そうな/に / な-Adj + そうな/に
en.notes: いい→よさそう, ない→なさそう.
examples[].german: That's a delicious-looking cake.
He's laughing cheerfully.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: Before a noun you need そうな.
The copula does not come before ケーキ as a modifier here.
The attributive form is そうな.

en.explanation: すぎる with adjectives: an excessively strong quality.
en.formation: い-Adj (without い) + すぎる / な-Adj + すぎる
en.notes: Conjugates like an ichidan verb.
examples[].german: This room is too hot.
It's so quiet it's scary.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: The final い is dropped before すぎる.
だ does not follow the verb すぎる.
The form attaches directly to 暑 here.

en.explanation: 間に: at some point within a period of time. 間: for the whole duration.
en.formation: Verb (ている) + 間(に) / Noun + の間(に)
en.notes: 間に = at a point. 間 = throughout.
examples[].german: I cleaned while my mother was sleeping.
I was traveling during the summer vacation.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This means before the vacation.
This means after the vacation.
This is not a temporal noun connection.

en.explanation: 後で and てから: after an action.
en.formation: Verb (た形) + 後で / Verb (て) + から
en.notes: てから puts more emphasis on the sequence.
examples[].german: Let's go for a drink after work.
I'll go out after eating.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: 前に requires the dictionary form and means before.
ながら requires the verb stem.
終わったてから is not a valid verb connection.

en.explanation: 合う as a suffix: an action is done mutually.
en.formation: Verb (ます-stem) + 合う
en.notes: 話し合う (to discuss), 助け合う (to help each other), 愛し合う (to love each other).
examples[].german: My friends and I help each other.
Let's discuss this problem.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: This negates the mutual help.
合う forms the て-form 合って.
ます is not inserted between the verbs.

en.explanation: ば-form: a hypothetical condition.
en.formation: Godan: u→eba / Ichidan: る→れば
en.notes: する→すれば, 来る→来れば. ～ば～ほど = the more ..., the more ....
examples[].german: If I have time, I'll go.
If it's cheap, I'll buy it.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: あれたら is not a conditional form of ある.
あれなら is not a form of ある here.
あれても is not a verb form.

en.explanation: ばよかった: regret about something you didn't do.
en.formation: Verb (ば-form) + よかった
en.notes: Negative: ～なければよかった (shouldn't have done it).
examples[].german: I should have studied more.
I should have brought an umbrella.
examples[].cloze.quiz.distractors[].reas: すれたら is not a verb form.
This does not express regret in hindsight.
よい forms its past as よかった.

en.explanation: ばかり expresses that someone does something exclusively or excessively.
en.formation: Verb (て-form) + ばかり / Noun + ばかり
en.notes: With the た-form it means "just (now)": 来たばかり = just arrived.
examples[].german: He does nothing but play games.
Don't eat only sweet things.
